name: Ruben Gallego
subject: My 2 cents on the “Arc de Trump”
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
With everything that’s going on, I can’t believe we have to talk about this
#

**Trump-Appointed Commission Approves Plan for 250 Foot Tall “Arc de Trump”**
Peter, I can’t believe we have to talk about this, but if you have a moment, I have some more personal feelings about this that I’d like to share with you.
As you know, I was an infantryman in Lima Company, 3rd Battalion, 25th Marines. We fought in Anbar, Iraq. They called us “Lucky Lima” because we didn’t have a single casualty in the first two months of our deployment.
Our luck didn’t hold though. By the time our deployment was over, we had more casualties than any unit in the Iraq War.
I joined the Marines to serve my country, but I ran for Senate for the guys I served with. They’ve been let down too many times, and I ran to change that.
This arch is an insult to those who have served. It will tower over Arlington National Cemetery, literally casting Donald Trump’s shadow over men and women who have made the ultimate sacrifice for their country.
All this from the man who received multiple deferments when his country called on him to serve, and called POW’s “suckers and losers.”
I would like to try to stop this project – or at least let my colleagues know what a mistake it is. **And I would like you to join me in that effort – so when they ask, I can tell them it's not just me, it's people everywhere who are rising in opposition.**
[**Please add your name to tell Congress – my colleagues – you oppose the “Arc de Trump.” No man’s ego should obscure the sacrifice of those who have served.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260520-arc-de-trump-em/?source=em260529-1-EOM&refcode2=4143.734936.5x7iGK&akid=4143%2E734936%2E5x7iGK)

Semper Fi,
Ruben

name: Public Land Warriors
subject: Steve Pearce wants to mine the Grand Canyon
body:
We're disgusted

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/7e7Qw8oAfvHFdgXVi746kw~~/AAUS1hA~/Yb0ewK5DqkxoTtEbMGMStWMAH-Y87dfqSkHzOL9XZm218XAUEsGGZP_cJCUV6iQDnv-lBk4kMsFZHgCSad_H1uGs0CgJWzkcLUvs095skg_MRQQssEbVFgdw8kRr42ko)
| | | | Peter, Last week, the Senate confirmed Steve Pearce to lead the Bureau of Land Management. The man now in charge of a quarter-billion acres of your public land and 700 million acres of underground minerals is a career politician deeply beholden to the oil, gas, and mining industries. While in Congress, he actively pushed to shrink national monuments like the Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks just to appease developers. And now, his agenda is clear: **unravel conservation plans, open millions of acres of public lands to corporate extraction, and most egregiously,****open the Grand Canyon up for mining.** That is not an exaggeration. The administration is actively plotting to roll back protections and hand the sacred and fragile lands surrounding one of the natural wonders of the world over to the mining lobby. We are officially putting every single politician who voted for this disastrous confirmation on notice. If they think they can hand the Grand Canyon— _one of the most beautiful places not just in this country, but on planet Earth_ —over to a mining conglomerate without ending their political careers, they don't know who they are dealing with. [**Will you channel your anger into action and chip in $25, $50, or $100 today to help Public Land Warriors fund the rapid-response backlash and protect the Grand Canyon from the auction block?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/rpUdrjq2zZiYVUaxvXko4g~~/AAUS1hA~/G7Y9BE1qkNLxVZTxUIfXW-wn8SIQ87FmWL7UGbKJC0od2H4ai56uMKmiqoH-gR9o8qNZ2_qj30ce7Q5mmk1d0A5SYs-TcvmaUA52ztdAZc0WsgMApCJlv3MfplLeROAevA0fxeWeIvsP9Bs7gUsAL4ub3u9T32p8JEszMhroPHx7rV7-ITesgEO008PPpDlflAHiDuZImxi6v-genS56abpGOGN8shomVVGYonD5M9ZAek29jt9VqGA7AFUb2yYR) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/rpUdrjq2zZiYVUaxvXko4g~~/AAUS1hA~/G7Y9BE1qkNLxVZTxUIfXW-wn8SIQ87FmWL7UGbKJC0od2H4ai56uMKmiqoH-gR9o8qNZ2_qj30ce7Q5mmk1d0A5SYs-TcvmaUA52ztdAZc0WsgMApCJlv3MfplLeROAevA0fxeWeIvsP9Bs7gUsAL4ub3u9T32p8JEszMhroPHx7rV7-ITesgEO008PPpDlflAHiDuZImxi6v-genS56abpGOGN8shomVVGYonD5M9ZAek29jt9VqGA7AFUb2yYR) ** You take our land, we take your seat. Peter -

I read this line from the Cook Political Report on Monday and it stopped me:

"An increasingly sour national environment for Republicans."

They moved Georgia and North Carolina from toss up to lean Democrat. Ohio slipped from lean R to toss up. Three races against us in one morning.

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, we are
officially four days away from the Democratic primary elections in New
Jersey and California — and we have the chance to send FOUR more Justice
Democrats to Congress.

But corporate Democrats, AIPAC, billionaire dollars, and establishment
super PACs are spending heavily to stop them.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260529-1.lvnJts&refcode=em20260529-37835&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37835%2E1203867%2E1f9Jea ]If you’re already with us, can you rush $5 or more right
now to get our candidates in NJ and CA over the finish line on Tuesday,
June 2?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260529-1.lvnJts&refcode=em20260529-37835&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37835%2E1203867%2E1f9Jea ]Contribute $5

In New Jersey, Dr. Adam Hamawy is taking on the political establishment in
NJ-12 with a campaign rooted in healthcare justice, ending forever wars,
and fighting for working people over corporate interests.

And in California, three more bold progressives are running against deeply
entrenched establishment power backed by AIPAC and the AI lobby:

* Mai Vang in CA-07, a Sacramento City Councilmember and daughter of
Hmong refugees who is taking on a nearly 50-year Matsui political
dynasty with a campaign focused on working families and community
investment;
* Angela Gonzales-Torres in CA-34, a working-class Angeleno and
community advocate who is challenging incumbent Jimmy Gomez with a
movement centered on affordable housing, public safety, and economic
justice;
* And Saikat Chakrabarti in CA-11, a former Bernie Sanders organizer and
co-founder of Justice Democrats, who is running to succeed Nancy
Pelosi with a bold vision for climate action, holding Big Tech
accountable, and ending corruption in politics.

Every single one of these candidates is rejecting corporate PAC money and
focused on building grassroots power — and they’re exactly what the
establishment is afraid of.

While their opponents have corporate PACs, AIPAC, and party insiders
lining up behind them — our candidates have YOU.

These races are about more than just four seats in Congress. They’re about
whether the Democratic Party will continue protecting a broken status quo
— or become a party that will actually fight for working people.

Right now, too many establishment Democrats offer the same old talking
points and fail to act, while families struggle with impossible rents,
unaffordable healthcare, stagnant wages, and the consequences of endless
war.

Our Justice Democrats are running to change that.

But with just one week left until these primaries, we need the resources
to fight back against the flood of attacks and outside spending pouring
into these races.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260529-1.lvnJts&refcode=em20260529-37835&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37835%2E1203867%2E1f9Jea ]So please, Peter,
chip in whatever you can today to help
elect FOUR more Justice Democrats on Tuesday and transform the party as we
know it. Every dollar in this final stretch matters.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260529-1.lvnJts&refcode=em20260529-37835&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37835%2E1203867%2E1f9Jea ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

body:
Support from legislators across Louisiana highlights continued momentum in U.S. Senate runoff campaign

| | |

| | | | [|

| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMay 29, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**FORTY LOUISIANA STATE REPRESENTATIVES ENDORSE JULIA LETLOW FOR U.S. SENATE** _Support from legislators across Louisiana highlights continued momentum in U.S. Senate runoff campaign_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed conservative candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced endorsements from 40 members of the Louisiana House of Representatives.
The endorsements come as Letlow continues to build support from conservative leaders across the state ahead of the Republican Senate runoff election.
The endorsing Representatives include:

* Speaker Phillip DeVillier* (District 41)
* Tony Bacala (District 59)
* Larry Bagley (District 7)
* Dennis Bamburg (District 5)
* Mike Bayham (District 103)
* Gerald "Beau" Beaullieu, IV (District 48)
* Stephanie Hunter Berault (District 76)
* Dewith Carrier (District 32)
* Kim Carver (District 89)
* Emily Chenevert (District 66)
* Vincent E. Cox, III (District 85)
* Daryl Deshotel (District 28)
* Jessica Domangue (District 53)
* Peter Egan (District 74)
* Bryan Fontenot (District 55)
* Foy Gadberry (District 15)
* Brian Glorioso (District 90)
* Troy Hebert (District 31)
* John Illg (District 78)
* Tim Kerner (District 84)
* Jacob Landry (District 49)
* Shane Mack* (District 95)
* Jack McFarland (District 13)
* Dixon McMakin (District 68)
* Michael Melerine (District 6)
* Nicholas Muscarello (District 86)
* Joseph Orgeron (District 54)
* Neil Riser (District 20)
* Paul Sawyer (District 69)
* Laurie Schlegel (District 82)
* Annie Spell (District 45)
* Polly Thomas (District 80)
* Christopher Turner (District 12)
* Lauren Ventrella (District 65)
* Debbie Villio (District 79)
* Roger Wilder* (District 71)
* Jeff Wiley (District 81)
* Mark Wright (District 77)
* John Wyble (District 75)
* Jerome Zeringue (District 52)

_* = Previously announced_
_“I’m honored to have the support of these conservative leaders from every corner of Louisiana,”_**said Congresswoman Letlow.** _“They know what is at stake in this election and understand that Louisiana needs a senator who will stand with President Trump, fight for the America First agenda, and never waver when it matters most. I’m grateful for their trust and support, and I look forward to continuing to earn the support of voters across our state.”_
The endorsements add to the growing list of elected officials, conservative organizations, and community leaders supporting Letlow’s campaign for the United States Senate. President Donald Trump endorsed Letlow's candidacy earlier this year, calling her a “strong conservative fighter” who will put Louisiana and America First.

body:
This move by the USPS would give the Trump admin unprecedented power over elections and it is cartoonishly unconstitutional.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fqO_yIvhWQEeIoUdqedbcy8U-JO6XGguy3840jsbeDD2Qt_vIaNbxeW_QUnUEyI65y1wGJZMRZv-bNn1-GfQW0ehbUeOFgVT8RTU6_ZT26OKFCByglnaKXXmq78i-8SotBBKhMGP5UOlGoSXKf55n6KyB6BxQPYdwUR2xzD_2Q_KBDyas64NtKBoU-b4fFtLB43-mB21Z2kIQmGxb18BYKDIw0EqkBuB&c=F1lWbq0BAbvAAHF1IQM2a8CF2u7kesUF9J2Z-Le29eFv4J8wY-56NQ==&ch=20tdD5aaTsjC7R1kSDm7tRfTRVCo8prfd-5JH9ruL_leAkL18CeW-A==)

|
Peter,
It was just revealed that the U.S. Postal Service is moving forward with a plan to limit mail-in voting by only sending ballots to voters who are registered on a list approved by the federal government.
This is an unprecedented assault for free and fair elections.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001fqO_yIvhWQEeIoUdqedbcy8U-JO6XGguy3840jsbeDD2Qt_vIaNbxeW_QUnUEyI65y1wGJZMRZv-bNn1-GfQW0ehbUeOFgVT8RTU6_ZT26OKFCByglnaKXXmq78i-8SotBBKhMGP5UOlGoSXKf55n6KyB6BxQPYdwUR2xzD_2Q_KBDyas64NtKBoU-b4fFtLB43-mB21Z2kIQmGxb18BYMYt7peTMRbe&c=F1lWbq0BAbvAAHF1IQM2a8CF2u7kesUF9J2Z-Le29eFv4J8wY-56NQ==&ch=20tdD5aaTsjC7R1kSDm7tRfTRVCo8prfd-5JH9ruL_leAkL18CeW-A==)
---
This rule would effectively give the Trump admin control over who receives ballots and who doesn't.
We do not have to imagine how Trump uses this power. Live in a heavily Democratic area? No ballot. Have a name that sounds Black or Hispanic? No ballot. They are not hiding what this is. It is a purge designed to look like election administration.
And that last part is particularly important. If you've been following our work, you know that in the Constitution, states have the responsibility for how elections are administered, not the federal government. This move by the USPS would give the Trump admin unprecedented power over elections and it is cartoonishly unconstitutional.
But legal challenges to this rule will likely make their way up to the Supreme Court. And that's where it gets scary--we have seen how this court has ruled lately. They have exposed themselves as complete and total puppets for Trump and MAGA extremists, willing to reverse nearly a half-century of legal precedent to tilt elections in their favor.
This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We are fighting on two fronts: building a firewall of state Supreme Courts that can protect free and fair elections at the state level, and building the movement to reform a federal court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.
[We need every Democrat who understands what is at stake to stand with us. body:
(This email is a little longer than usual. If you’re short on time, I hope you’ll split a donation between me and Tim Kaine ahead of our end-of-month fundraising deadline. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25] Every donation we receive before May ends puts us in a stronger position in the final months ahead of the midterms.)
Derek –
When I decided to run for reelection to the U.S. Senate, it was not a decision I made lightly. Asking Virginians to rehire me is a humbling task – and it’s one that I take very seriously.
But Derek, after seeing the crazed, dangerous, and callous actions of the second Trump term, I’m all-in on this race.
In my time in public service, I’ve never seen anything like I have the last sixteen months. Trump’s policies are skyrocketing prices for working families. They’re stripping health care away from millions of Americans to pay for tax breaks for those at the very top. And their reckless foreign policy is making our country less safe. And all the while, I’ve been disappointed to see too many of my Republican colleagues refuse to take any meaningful action to hold Trump and his reckless administration accountable.
But frankly, I also know that this race has to be about more than simply what we’re against – we need a vision of what we’re fighting for .
I’m running for reelection to not only continue standing up to the Trump administration’s chaos and corruption, but to also deliver real results for Virginia’s families:
→ We need universal health care in this country. I’ve long supported Obamacare, but simply patching up the old system isn’t cutting it anymore for the families who can’t pay their hospital bills or for life-saving prescriptions.
→ Virginians are facing a housing affordability crisis. We need to build more housing, rehabilitate existing structures, speed up permitting, and make it easier for first-time home buyers to obtain a mortgage.
→ We need to prepare our workforce for the economies of the future – making sure working Americans benefit from the good that could come from Artificial Intelligence and make sure Big Tech pays their fair share for the demand they’re placing on our energy grid.
→ We’ve got to stand up for America’s critical role in the world. That means working with our allies – not against them – and restoring our leadership on the world stage.
Folks, there’s no doubt these are big challenges – but I’ve never been afraid of a tough fight, and I know you aren’t either.
So here’s the deal: my campaign is coming up on our end-of-month fundraising deadline and we’ve set an ambitious goal of raising $50,000 from grassroots donors like you before the month ends.
These fundraising benchmarks are critical for my fight to protect this Senate seat and elect Democrats in all corners of the Commonwealth to flip the balance of power in Washington. Your support determines what kinds of resources we have in the months ahead, and they guide the strategic decisions we’re making now to put us in a strong position come the fall.
So I’m asking: can I count on your support today to help us reach our fundraising goal? Your donation will be split between my campaign and Tim Kaine's. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
DONATE $25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?express_lane=true&amount=25]
DONATE $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?express_lane=true&amount=50]
DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?express_lane=true&amount=100]
OTHER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25]
I’m proud to be in this fight – and I’m thankful that you’re with me.
– Mark Warner

Trump promised lower costs, we’re still waiting

George Latimer is a lifelong Westchester resident who has built a career in public service by delivering unparalleled progressive results for local residents. Now, he's taking that work to the next level by serving as your Congressman, representing New York's 16th District. Back in March, I stopped at the gas station 3 blocks from my home to fill up the tank of our family car. The price for regular gas was $4.19 per gallon. Less than 2 weeks ago, I stopped at that very same gas station and filled up again, but this time, gas was $4.79 per gallon. _That’s 60 cents more per gallon in just 50 days — a $12 increase overall._ Standing at the pump, I couldn’t help but think about folks in our community who are struggling with the rising cost of living under this administration. Donald Trump and his cronies can shrug off an extra $12 at the pump — but what about the waitress driving home after a late shift, the home health aide driving from one patient's home to the next, or the truck driver watching fuel costs eat into every paycheck? Donald Trump promised to make life more affordable. But people can see with their own eyes that costs are still climbing, and working families are footing the bill. And here’s the thing, Peter: Republicans are more focused on scoring political points by blaming Joe Biden, Barack Obama, and every Democrat going back to FDR and Grover Cleveland than lowering costs for working families. Despite the hyperpartisanship in Washington, I’m fighting every day in Congress to deliver results over rhetoric. But we need to build the resources _now_ to keep this seat, support vulnerable House Democrats, and put a critical check on Donald Trump’s power. **[If you’re with me, will you chip in $10, or anything you can afford before my upcoming end–of-month deadline?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132314136/624109524/446446218?amount=10&source=GL_EM_FR_052926_B1_EOM01&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQwMzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDVjYzQ5MmItN2I1Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=a-OSNk2ogcgY4XBOey6-YuOhRLDLGdTMgPGpfwT2O0o=)** | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now.

Less than 2 weeks ago, I stopped at that very same gas station and filled up again, but this time, gas was $4.79 per gallon. That’s 60 cents more per gallon in just 50 days — a $12 increase overall. Standing at the pump, I couldn’t help but think about folks in our community who are struggling with the rising cost of living under this administration. Donald Trump and his cronies can shrug off an extra $12 at the pump — but what about the waitress driving home after a late shift, the home health aide driving from one patient's home to the next, or the truck driver watching fuel costs eat into every paycheck? Donald Trump promised to make life more affordable. But people can see with their own eyes that costs are still climbing, and working families are footing the bill. And here’s the thing, Peter: Republicans are more focused on scoring political points by blaming Joe Biden, Barack Obama, and every Democrat going back to FDR and Grover Cleveland than lowering costs for working families. name: Trina Swanson
subject: I’m rooted here in Minnesota.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Trina for Congress
body:
trinaforcongress.com [trinaforcongress.com]
Friends,
I grew up in Hermantown, worked for years in Minnesota, and was honored to represent the United States in countries around the world to ensure our borders were protected while upholding our democratic values. While I was far away from family in miles, my heart was always in the Northland. I’m not a political insider — I’m just someone who knows that our northern and central Minnesota communities deserve a leader who puts them first.
Our campaign must meet our grassroots fundraising goals to fund our organizing efforts. With just two days left until the end of the month, we’re $3,362 short of reaching our end-of-month goal. Can you please donate $25 to help us bridge the gap? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trina-swanson-may-email?&amount=25&refcode=20260529]
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trina-swanson-may-email?&amount=25&refcode=20260529]
I’m rooted here in Minnesota, and I know that the proud folks around here aren’t looking for a handout or a giveaway. Our workers just want jobs that pay the bills, put food on the table, and allow them to save a few bucks for a rainy day. Our families want to know that the rural hospital they rely on isn’t suddenly going to close or cut services. And regardless of political belief or background, we ALL want to be able to fill up our gas tanks without having to worry about cutting back on something else.
For too long, Pete Stauber has ignored our district’s very real needs so that he can cozy up to the same special interests who are taking advantage of our rural communities. He has some rich and powerful friends who are ready to bankroll his campaign, but he’s not as strong as he pretends.
We’re counting on supporters like you to help us build a campaign with the strength to win, and we appreciate anything you can give. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trina-swanson-may-email?&amount=25&refcode=20260529]

clean_body: They were elected to serve us, but the only person they serve is Trump. | = Peter, Republicans hold a razor-thin majority in Congress — and they’re using it to protect Trump, enable his corruption, and push his agenda. Instead of making life safer or more affordable for working families, congressional Republicans have made their top priorities clear: keeping Trump in power and helping his allies cash in. Just look at what they’re defending, popularity with voters be damned: A $1.8 billion slush fund to pay out criminals and Trump’s MAGA cronies without a trial. Thousands of stock trades made in Trump’s name while he’s been in office. Repeated threats to investigate, indict, and even execute his political rivals. ...and the list goes on. As unpopular as Trump’s corruption is with the American people, congressional Republicans refuse to do anything about it. They’re not even TRYING to hold him accountable. They’re trying to keep him in power because it benefits them. = | = Congressional Republicans no longer see their job as serving their constituents. U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson even admitted that his primary concern for the midterms is whether Republicans can keep empowering Trump’s agenda — saying that if Republicans lose the House, it would effectively end Trump’s presidency. He’s right to be worried. Our candidates have dedicated their careers to serving their families, their neighbors, and their communities. They’re running to lower costs, protect our rights, defend our democracy, and fight for everyday people — not the rich and powerful, not Trump, not his megadonors, and not the special interests cashing in on his corruption. Friend, The latest midterm forecasts are showing something Republicans never thought they’d see: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132316840/624118106/-1340403166?refcode=AU_MTH_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260529_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMTY2YTdkYy03ZjViLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=KMLk3Ps4GrXdwBs166sBiWygWR5vN_h86vcxzmOQ-1I=) **Democrats now have a real shot at taking back both the House and the Senate. VoteHub forecasts that Democrats have a nearly 50% chance of flipping both chambers.** _And honestly? It’s not hard to understand why._ Working families are getting hammered by rising costs. At the same time, Republicans in Washington focus on tax breaks for the wealthy, endless political theater, and reckless foreign conflicts that make life even more expensive here at home. **Gas prices are up.** **Groceries cost more.** **Home ownership feels out of reach for more and more people.** Meanwhile, Trump and his allies in Congress are acting like the rules don’t apply to them.
That’s why taking back the House and Senate matters so much. We need leaders who will hold this administration accountable and fight for the people actually struggling to pay bills—not billionaires or corporate executives. Andrew Schultz said something this week that honestly explains the entire problem with modern American politics better than most elected officials ever could:
By ousting Thomas Massie in the Kentucky Senate primary, Republican voters appeared to validate one of the most common stereotypes coastal elites hold about Southern Republican voters: that they are easily persuaded to vote against their own interests.
And before conservatives get angry about that, listen to what he actually meant.
* * *
_**Today 's rant is sponsored by Incogni.**_
Someone just looked you up. You had no idea.
A researcher at [Consumer Reports](https://substack.com/redirect/04bde2c8-3f13-41dd-bded-ac6319e7480a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--someone whose job is online safety--typed her own name into a search engine. Her home address, age, and phone number were sitting there, on data broker sites she'd never heard of. No hack. No breach. Just her name in a search box.
Yours is there too. Right now. Available to an ex, a stranger, anyone who decides they want to find you.
That's why my team and I use [Incogni.](https://substack.com/redirect/9e51c5cb-f51a-4833-a093-d4e3eee6f0a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) It's one of those things you don't realize you need until you see how much of your life is just...publicly available online.
_**[Incogni removes your data from those sites and keeps it off. Try Incogni today and get 55% off annual plans with code MIKE.](https://substack.com/redirect/1771d633-6eb8-4dc5-9f2d-a3538ca2451f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[ Check out Incogni](https://substack.com/redirect/9e51c5cb-f51a-4833-a093-d4e3eee6f0a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Schulz' comment wasn't about mocking working-class people or rural voters or pretending Democrats are morally or intellectually superior. It was about manipulation.
Kentucky voters didn't suddenly become less intelligent than voters anywhere else. They were targeted by one of the most sophisticated political influence operations ever deployed in a congressional race. Tens of millions of dollars were spent flooding voters with AI-generated garbage, fake outrage, and loyalty tests until they turned on one of the few Republicans in Congress who actually believe in something.
And honestly, this should terrify everybody; regardless of what party you side with.
Because the Thomas Massie situation isn't really about Thomas Massie. **It 's the first glimpse of what politics looks like when AI-powered propaganda becomes more powerful than ideology itself.**
We're rapidly entering an era where billionaires, super PACs, influencers, algorithms, and synthetic media can manufacture reality for voters -- and punish anyone who refuses to participate in or pushes back against it.
That's the real story here.
Let me be clear: Massie is not a liberal. He's not some secret Democrat. He's a conservative libertarian from Kentucky who voted with Republicans the overwhelming majority of the time. Full stop.
But that is exactly what makes this story so important:**Massie didn 't change. The **_**rules**_**changed.** The moment he criticized Trump on Iran, government spending, and the Epstein files, the machine turned on him instantly.
And the way they destroyed him says everything about what politics is becoming.
Outside groups dumped roughly $35 million into the Kentucky Congressional race while flooding voters with AI-generated attack ads portraying Massie in fake sexual scenarios with AOC and Ilhan Omar.
Think about how insane that is for a second.
We are now entering an era where political campaigns can generate completely fabricated imagery at scale, push it through partisan media ecosystems, microtarget emotionally vulnerable voters, and then hide behind shell PACs with names designed to sound grassroots and local.
And millions of people will believe it.
That's psychological warfare with better software operating in a dysfunctional democracy. But the most terrifying part of all of this it that it _worked_. That's the lesson every campaign consultant, billionaire donor, PAC strategist, and political operative just learned.
And what's wild is that even Schultz -- somebody who spent years inside the broader anti-establishment media ecosystem, who helped bolster Trump -- seems genuinely disturbed by how openly manipulative this has become. He basically says Kentucky voters got conned by a machine designed to prey on emotion instead of reality.
Honestly, I think a lot of people across the political spectrum know that feeling now.
Because whether it's Fox News, TikTok politics, left-wing influencer culture, MAGA podcasts, partisan YouTube channels, or algorithmic outrage farming, _everybody_ is being pushed into increasingly artificial versions of reality where nuance and critical thinking disappear completely.
Massie voted against Republican spending bills because he believed they would increase the country's debt (which they do--the "Big Beautiful Budget" blew a multi-trillion-dollar hole in the deficit) and somehow that reasoning became "Massie sides with AOC." And that machine-generated narrative spread like wildfire across social media.
The goal wasn't to convince voters that Massie was wrong. **The goal was to convince them that he was disloyal.** And that's a completely different kind of politics. One is about ideas. The other is about blind obedience where questioning war becomes disloyalty and where questioning Trump becomes treason.
That's the part I think people are underestimating.
The modern Republican Party is no longer really organized around conservative ideology. It's organized around loyalty to Trump and the media ecosystem surrounding him. The second somebody deviates from that ecosystem -- even slightly -- they become disposable regardless of their actual record.
And Democrats should be careful before they laugh too hard about this because the same incentives exist everywhere now. It affects the left just as much of the right.
The internet rewards emotional manipulation more than truth. Outrage spreads faster than complexity. Algorithms reward certainty, anger, humiliation, and fear because those emotions keep people online longer.
That's why politics increasingly feels like professional wrestling mixed with behavioral psychology.
And AI is about to make all of it exponentially worse.
Because most people are not equipped to navigate a world where fake images, fake audio, fake video, and synthetic narratives become indistinguishable from reality. Especially older voters who already struggle with basic internet misinformation.
This isn't meant to be an insult. It's simply true.
And honestly, I think the generational divide Schultz talks about is real. Younger voters grew up understanding that the internet manipulates you. Older generations often still consume media as if the traditional gatekeepers (Fox, CNN, etc.) are fundamentally trustworthy.
Except now the gatekeepers are influencers, PACs, billionaire and corporate-owned media conglomerates, anonymous meme accounts, and AI-generated content farms.
That's a dangerous combination.
And underneath all of this is an even bigger problem that nobody in power seems interested in fixing: the collapse of trust in the institutions that are supposed to help us distinguish truth from fiction.
People don't trust the press.
They don't trust Congress.
They don't trust universities.
They don't trust the justice system.
And increasingly, they don't trust reality itself.
That vacuum creates the perfect environment for political cults, conspiracy theories, and authoritarian personalities who promise certainty in an age where everything feels unstable.
That's why this Massie story matters even if you disagree with him politically.
Because once a political system starts rewarding absolute loyalty over independent thought, it inevitably becomes more extreme, more dishonest, and more disconnected from reality over time.
And AI-driven propaganda is only going to accelerate that collapse.
The scary part is that this is probably still the early version.
Right now the fake images are sloppy enough that people can still sometimes tell they're fake. Give it a few more years and they may become near indistinguishable. Eventually voters won't be able to distinguish reality from fabrication at all unless they actively spend time verifying information themselves.
Most people won't do that.
They'll just believe whatever confirms their emotional biases the fastest. And the algorithms in our feeds know that.
And whichever political movement learns to weaponize that environment most effectively is probably going to dominate the next era of American politics.
Not because they're right or because they have better ideas, but because they understand modern media better than everybody else.
That's the future we're walking into right now.
And honestly, I don't think the country is prepared for it.
**The real lesson of the Massie story isn 't what happened to Thomas Massie.** It's that millions of dollars, AI-generated propaganda, and a loyalty-driven media machine were able to convince voters that one of the most conservative members of Congress was somehow their enemy. **If that can happen to him, it can happen to anyone.** And once politics becomes a competition to manufacture reality instead of debate reality, democracy stops being a contest of ideas and becomes a contest of influence.

body:
I'm looking for your personal endorsement
#
Friend, now that we've elected Chris Taylor to Wisconsin's Supreme Court, all eyes have shifted to our August election.
This is a longer email, but I'm not going to ask you for money—[**just your grassroots endorsement.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=1&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)
**I wanted to take this chance to reintroduce myself: my name is David Crowley, I'm running for Wisconsin Governor, and there's a lot at stake for working people.**
**[ENDORSE DAVID ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=2&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)**
I know firsthand that when systems fail, families feel it first.
My family certainly did.
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=3&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)
My father worked as an electrician, and my mother worked in the service industry, while both battled addiction and mental health struggles.
I spent many days at school wondering if I’d come home to find our belongings on the curb after another eviction, and I quickly learned what it was like to come home to no food in the kitchen and no heat in the house.
**Those experiences shaped me, and they’re why I’ve dedicated my life to public service.**
Today, as a husband and father of three, I’m laser-focused on what policy really means at the kitchen table.
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=4&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)
That means fighting for:

**➡️ Affordable, safe housing across Wisconsin**
**➡️ Health care that reaches people**
**➡️ Accessible childcare for Wisconsin families**
**➡️ Jobs and wages that build futures for working-class folks**
**➡️ Expanding the middle class**
My lived experience is how I lead, friend. I understand that the challenges families face aren’t only policy debates, but they're the everyday realities so many folks in Wisconsin are facing.
**That’s the mindset I’ve brought as a State Representative, as Milwaukee County Executive, and now as a candidate for Governor.**
[**Friend, I’m ready to fight for a Wisconsin where every family has the chance to thrive—but I need your support to do it. Will you endorse our campaign today to help us kick off in the right way?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=5&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)
**[ADD YOUR NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22740?t=6&akid=1643%2E2118727%2EdUe3ek)**
Thank you,
David Crowley

As your next Lieutenant Governor, I am honored and proud to share we have been recognized as winners in the 47th Telly Awards for our Social Impact series with Teen Kids News, _The Covid Generation_.
This project tackled one of the most important conversations facing America today: the lasting impact of isolation, social media, disrupted education, and mental health challenges on our youth.
Our mission has always been to spark meaningful dialogue, inspire leadership, and remind young people that resilience, purpose, and community still matter.
Thank you to everyone who helped bring this message to life. Together, we continue to invest in the next generation of leaders.
Respectfully,Dr. Josh McConkey

body:
President Trump and his family are milking the cow that is America all while Middle Class Americans are paying more in every part of their lives.
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2461%2E135344%2EZg558p)

President Trump and his family are milking the cow that is America all while Middle Class Americans are paying more in every part of their lives.
But it is not only Republicans that have failed.
The last election was about the cost of living in America and as Democrats, we totally whiffed it. We took our eye off the ball. When you try to focus on everything, you prioritize nothing -- and the focus right now has to be rising costs and what it takes to build things in this country.
Overregulation is one issue Democrats must address if we are going to make things more affordable in this country.
**[Let me explain.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4376?t=2&akid=2461%2E135344%2EZg558p)**
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4376?t=3&akid=2461%2E135344%2EZg558p)
Thanks for watching,
Elissa Slotkin

* * *

As one of the few Senators who won a Senate race in the same state won by Trump, Elissa Slotkin is being asked to campaign for other Democrats in tough races across the country this election.
And while Elissa wishes we did not have to send another email asking you to contribute, that is what we have to do today.
The outcome of this election will determine whether we are able to put a check on President Trump during the final two years of his term. We have to take back the House and the Senate. And we need your help to get it done.

name: Rashida Tlaib
subject: BREAKING: We have not one, but two opponents in our Democratic primary
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
At least one of our opponents has a history of working for billionaires and taking money from oil lobbyists, the banking industry, and DTE energy.
Peter,
**We recently learned that we will have not one, but two opponents in our Democratic primary.** But with neither having filed a required fundraising report with the Federal Election Commission, it leads us to ask, _who is funding them?_
**At least one of our opponents has a history of working for billionaires and corporate polluters while accepting money from oil lobbyists, the banking industry, and DTE Energy.**
Voters deserve a voice in Congress who will always put their interests ahead of Big Money and the billionaire bullies. And that’s what I’ve done throughout my career fighting for you.
In the past, people have been offered tens of millions of dollars to run against me. **With less than three months until Election Day, I need your urgent support right now.**
[**Split $10 today between my campaign and Abdul El-Sayed to show our opponents and their wealthy backers that we’re ready for the fight ahead.**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260529-2-ak.4bJ4qz&amount=10&refcode=em20260529-2254&t=2&akid=2254%2E251025%2EfxJ8Au)
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260529-2-ak.4bJ4qz&amount=10&refcode=em20260529-2254&t=21&akid=2254%2E251025%2EfxJ8Au)**
**Big Banks, greedy corporate polluters, and genocide enablers aren’t shy about funding my opponents. That’s because I haven’t been shy about taking on their special interests.**
I’m part of the House Financial Services Committee, where I’ve held executives at J.P. Morgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and CitiGroup accountable for how their investments in dirty fossil fuel projects are contributing to environmental racism.
They’ve poisoned our air, water, and soil in frontline communities, endangering our public health—and I’ll keep taking them on and fighting for environmental justice.
**Billionaires may spend millions funding my opponents too. That’s because I’ve never been afraid to take them on, including when I successfully pushed the Koch brothers to fully clean up and remove toxic waste from Detroit’s riverfront.**
We don’t need any more billionaire-funded politicians in Washington.
[**Let’s show that we’re ready for the fight ahead! Split a donation today to power my re-election campaign and let Michigan’s voters know that we’re fighting for them every single day.**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260529-2-ak.4bJ4qz&amount=10&refcode=em20260529-2254&t=22&akid=2254%2E251025%2EfxJ8Au)
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260529-2-ak.4bJ4qz&amount=10&refcode=em20260529-2254&t=41&akid=2254%2E251025%2EfxJ8Au)**
Together, we will show billionaire bullies that people power will always defeat their Big Money interests.
Always serving you,
Rashida

By sending these cases back to hostile lower courts, the conservative majority left this essential civil rights law on life support. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson rightly dissented, warning that the court should have firmly protected the rights of voters to stand up for themselves. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132319431/624126807/1254288483?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZmNjYjYwMjQtODM1Yi1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTg5MDVjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bylzUJIT4Hab8StyJWthVA3xpelzkoIqCTfuFSrdNTU=) Friend, Every day, whether Congress is “in session” or not, I am putting my best foot forward to find real, meaningful solutions to the challenges we’re facing. Pull up a chair — I just checked our latest finance stats and wanted to be straight with you about where we're at.

Hey,
I’ve spent the last two hours staring at the giant whiteboard in my office, trying to figure out how to stretch our budget just a _little bit further_ before the end-of-month deadline hits.
When you’re the Finance Director for a campaign like Mallory’s, your job is basically a giant logic puzzle. Every dollar that comes in gets instantly translated into real-world action: a couple bucks covers a tank of gas for a field organizer, twenty-five buys a stack of yard signs, and fifty keeps our voter outreach software online for another day.
Right now, the puzzle is missing a few pieces. We’re running just a bit short of the benchmark we need to hit by Friday night to keep our field expansion on schedule. [**Can you help with that?**](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-may2026._5OkES&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_EOM_AC_20260529_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=3&akid=4830%2E898137%2EZahjG2)

---
I’m telling you this because I think you deserve to see the actual math, not just receive another high-stress email pretending the sky is falling. The sky isn't falling — **the energy on the ground is actually incredible.** But the reality of running a campaign without a single dime of corporate PAC money means we don't have a safety net. Mallory answers to regular people, which is exactly how it should be, but it means we live and die by the generosity of this community.
If we want to keep our organizers out on the doors meeting voters face-to-face across Michigan, we have to close this gap in the next few days.
[**If you’re in a position to help us out today, could you chip in $10 or $25 to help us fill in those missing pieces on the whiteboard?**](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-may2026._5OkES&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_EOM_AC_20260529_AM1_V1_S1&email=&t=5&akid=4830%2E898137%2EZahjG2)

# [Dimon warns Mamdani: Ideology dooms mayors](https://substack.com/redirect/64470113-fd29-46de-9cdb-25fb70a46b70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon described a pleasant private meeting with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, **[warning that ideology can blind leaders to practical policy](https://substack.com/redirect/08d9a9b3-b106-4d24-af6e-e76eb2071819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and cause mayors to fail abysmally when running a city of 300,000 employees.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/08d9a9b3-b106-4d24-af6e-e76eb2071819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Mayors Risk Ideological Failure:** Dimon has seen some fail spectacularly when ideology overrides realistic, real-world policy while others grow successfully into the demanding role.
**Private Meeting Called Pleasant:** The CEO said he told Mamdani everything he wanted during their one-on-one session at JPMorgan headquarters and offered help with good initiatives.
**Policy Over Taxes Urged:** Dimon stressed good policy is free and politicians should fix existing rules rather than raise taxes or spend more to accelerate economic growth.
**City Competitiveness Highlighted:** Conversation focused on quality-of-life factors like crime, police, sanitation and hospitals alongside taxes, red tape cuts and public-private partnerships.

name: Molly Gray
subject: Protecting Vermonters from AI Data Centers — here's where I stand
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Peter,
I want you to know exactly where I stand.
The Governor vetoed H.727 [https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/H.727] yesterday — a bill that passed the legislature with overwhelming bi-partisan support and would give Vermont communities a real voice over large-scale AI data centers coming to Vermont.
I stand with our rural communities, working families, farmers and those caring for our land and environment. I stand with rate payers. I stand with those legislators working to get ahead of the harms we’re witnessing nationally from mega AI data centers.
The average new U.S. data center is projected to nearly double in size by 2028 [https://www.clf.org/newsroom/vermont-legislature-passes-one-of-the-nations-strongest-data-center-laws/] , and some facilities currently being planned would consume far more electricity annually than the entire state of Vermont. These utility costs get shifted directly to ratepayers. To Vermonters.
That’s exactly why legislators acted now, before large-scale projects inevitably come to our state. H.727 would establish a transparent regulatory process — giving communities and developers clearer expectations while protecting Vermonters from shouldering the burden.
Vermont is leading the nation on this. [https://www.clf.org/newsroom/vermont-legislature-passes-one-of-the-nations-strongest-data-center-laws/] The first state to pass legislation like this. That's something to be proud of.
I'm not against economic growth. But growth can't come at the expense of our rural communities, or the working families already stretched thin by energy costs.
If you agree, I'd ask two things:
1. Call your legislators and urge them to override this veto today. Call: 802-828-2228.
2. If you believe Vermonters deserve a fighter in the Lt. Governor's Office who will stand up for rural communities, working families, and protect the rights of every Vermonter, chip in to keep this campaign going. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mrg2026-em]
I’m running to do just that. There are no ceremonial offices.
Let’s protect Vermonters, let's win this fight.
Molly Gray
DONATE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mrg2026-em]

subject: I have a question for you.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:

Hi friend — I have a question for you. Have you ever needed something from your government and realized the only way to get it was to know the right person? A permit that took forever until someone pulled it from the pile. A meeting that got on the calendar because you knew someone to call. A problem that got solved not because the system worked, but because you happened to have access to someone who could _make_ it work. I’ve heard some version of this story in every community I’ve visited across Rhode Island on my campaign for LG. **And every time I hear it, I think: this is exactly what government is**** _NOT_****supposed to look like.** **Government is supposed to work for everyone. Not just the lobbyists and people with connections. Not just the people who know how to navigate the bureaucracy. Not just the people who’ve been doing this long enough to know which phone to call.** **That’s what I want for the LG’s office.** I want an office where the doors are actually open. Where the process is actually legible. Where you don’t need to “know a guy” to get your government to do its job.
---
**I’ve been calling this**** _“Schoolhouse Rock for grownups.”_******
---
|
---
Government is complicated, but it shouldn’t be mysterious. You should be able to understand how decisions get made, how to show up and be heard, and how to hold your officials accountable without needing an insider to translate. That's how I've been as a City Councilor, and it's how I'll be as Lt. Governor. Government shouldn’t be a _game_ you have to know how to play. **And while corruption coming out of Washington D.C. seems to be swallowing us whole, I’m out to make sure that’s not the case here in Rhode Island.**

Dear Fellow American, A fifth-grade girl traveled with her Colorado school on a field trip across the country.

You can probably imagine how she must have felt in the days and weeks leading up to the trip. Excited to spend a few days with her friends. Eager to visit a new place. And, sure, a bit nervous--it's a big deal to stay overnight in a place you've never been before, especially as an 11-year-old.

**Now imagine how she felt when she found out --already hundreds of miles from home and in her hotel room for the night--_that she was supposed to share a bed with a boy._**

Shocked. Confused. Uncomfortable.

She slipped into the bathroom to call her mom, who was thankfully on the trip with her. Her mom thought she must have misunderstood. She couldn't fathom that the school assigned her daughter to room overnight with a boy.

But it wasn't a misunderstanding. It was _ school policy_.

The policy says that students on overnight trips will be assigned rooms based on their "gender identity," not on biology. And the school refuses to notify parents or students of the policy, or if a student of the opposite sex is assigned to the room.

That means a girl can be assigned to share a hotel room with a boy who identifies as a girl, without mom and dad's--or the student's--knowledge or say.

**How would you feel if this happened to your child or grandchild?**

It shouldn't have to be said--but this is just **WRONG.**

It's common sense that girls and boys deserve to have their own private spaces. And if that privacy could be infringed upon, parents need to know so that they can make informed decisions for their children.

Families across the country are being harmed by policies like these. That's why the Waileses, along with three other Colorado families, are pushing back in a lawsuit--for their kids and many others like them.

How would you feel if this happened to your child or grandchild? It shouldn't have to be said--but this is just WRONG. It's common sense that girls and boys deserve to have their own private spaces. And if that privacy could be infringed upon, parents need to know so that they can make informed decisions for their children. Families across the country are being harmed by policies like these. That's why the Waileses, along with three other Colorado families, are pushing back in a lawsuit--for their kids and many others like them. Please raise your voice to say NO MORE to policies that deny truth and violate parents ' rights--and to protect kids from harmful policies that put gender ideology above their comfort and privacy. For truth, Sharon Supp Legal Counsel, Center for Parental Rights Alliance Defending Freedom P.S. Colorado parents are pushing back after the school district assigned their daughter to share a room with a boy. Alliance Defending Freedom 15100 N. 90th Street, Scottsdale, Arizona 85260

Friend,

You may not have seen this on the news. The liberal mainstream media buried it.

**Two years ago, the Biden administration cut a plea deal with the masterminds of 9/11.** Khalid Sheikh Mohammed. The men who planned the murder of nearly 3,000 Americans.

[](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=c47df7dde2fe43bfbcaf9aa698ef7cd4&_e=gtaOQhRBRjF9W34gkU0RJMA8wONmgKfuCVhQ9FEA2R6SljgaqCIvnSUrvAw8fVuPf6NzES4oes8dvQ77xDgS-sTIquLsMRtuC19kQj8sO8gDiVUD1nzYmxKxSieYgC09bL1wzj6BUYrViceD90UPGvf0geseH0pZfJUOqnO00V2nIxvzt4M3CB9K12UV6RJTkDdtiUeE1fIx1QS8kErjinW6DxyPj60f4mAl3avoIvQjpuUer_-om1Fj8rIONhF4zkc7uKM6q6qNovGbrOxdmeZH1B5oje-pe1sJfaHFFY1qsSZmNLAzmEGju3piv6KoJgQQKtDFVGPwc14C4D1QwwOCWFH6I2J2tEJXC9Bq-dVhuLAYQWeH_7HYj68OwfE67h34QKlYAKGR_N16lBUSG_B4E56TFCcJfHPW4LNvNRFEzPeAH6fxlaXR90Ve5GA19RPRiZkWHat9dQI0hF3cqPleg0NMY439KlwKirE-sWpf7eufDlxkDzwkpfiJHp92)
The deal would have spared them from the death penalty. They would have lived out their days in a cell, three meals a day, on the American taxpayer's dime.

_**I was sickened.**_

You see, on the morning of September 11, 2001, I was a law student sitting in evidence class. I walked out and watched the Towers fall on live TV. That day changed my life forever. I led American soldiers in Baghdad and Afghanistan because of what those terrorists did to our country.

[](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=c47df7dde2fe43bfbcaf9aa698ef7cd4&_e=gtaOQhRBRjF9W34gkU0RJMA8wONmgKfuCVhQ9FEA2R6SljgaqCIvnSUrvAw8fVuPf6NzES4oes8dvQ77xDgS-sTIquLsMRtuC19kQj8sO8gDiVUD1nzYmxKxSieYgC09bL1wzj6BUYrViceD90UPGvf0geseH0pZfJUOqnO00V0xOsPRJjjBuEKwIDN308T2qDcTZBTFo-6W4Q4Snpib3s1G2kRLabwLlILtiR7VFHjk-baR81s_otLJKWNtKApTibJzzvcI2K5MyUsZO_Kk-LZ7yLkXpeGqoINxmoVR0SbYdnruBCSkqZHAieMMssxbaPAvX9RNhlj07S2g5MsW9mbUZtxF12Yygixmu1CYvCcU86fE7luxXpas8eKlYcD1sJ3W2V2of_72L6wWI2j2XoF0I_LX8rlaJs5PtQJcDb3gfZ_qARmw3uz5N2uCG26KKm5zT6C5Zl6ZJTQzqMN0bB16mBxKtk636FNSu8BQ_2flDNM4sbhqr2vjJ7SHcAtQ)
_So when I heard about that plea deal, I went to work._

I introduced legislation to block it. I took to the Senate floor. I made sure the families of the victims had a voice in Washington that the Biden White House refused to give them.

**The plea deal was thrown out.**

But the fight is not over. The Radical Left still does not believe in accountability and harsh punishment for terrorists. They want to empty Guantanamo Bay. They want to release killers back onto the battlefield or even worse–into America.

**I will never forget. And as long as I am in the United States Senate, those terrorists will face justice. Period.**

name: AOC
subject: Sam Forstag
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Our fight is far more united than people understand.
#
Last night, I joined Sam Forstag at a rally in Missoula, Montana.
In Montana, understandably, there’s a lot of suspicion around a city girl. But it’s important for us to know that a lot of that is intended to divide us.
Because what big money doesn't want us to realize is that **our struggles are far more common than our landscapes are different**.
Before the rally kicked off, I asked Sam, “What are some of the issues that are especially resonant in this community?” And Sam was talking to me about housing.
He went on to tell me that Montana is the hardest hit and worst housing market in America. I was shocked to hear that, as a New Yorker.
He said, “When you look at the average cost of housing pegged to the average salary here, it’s impossible.”
What the folks dumping tons of money into congressional races like Sam’s don’t want us to see, is that **the same forces that pushed my family out of New York City are the same forces pushing families out of Montana**.
Our fight is far more united than people understand.
It’s really not even about blue, or red, or any of that. **This is about people who are accountable to everyday, working families** — who don’t take big money, but take your voice, and your input, and put that in the halls of power.
[Will you split a $5 contribution today between Sam and I — two candidates who take zero money from corporations or special interests _precisely_ so we are accountable only to the people who elect us?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260529-forstag.9ts18M&refcode=em20260529-11552-P_FND_SPL_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11552%2E2526796%2ET1hpP3)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260529-forstag.9ts18M&refcode=em20260529-11552-P_FND_SPL_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=20&akid=11552%2E2526796%2ET1hpP3)**
Sam has spent his life protecting Montana, and believes the people deserve a government that protects them, too.
Sam is a smokejumper. As it turns out, it is one of the most dangerous jobs there is: smokejumpers parachute out of small planes into wildfires that other firefighters can't reach, and work for days to keep the fire from reaching the next town.
That means something: when something is burning, Sam runs toward that fire. That’s who he is. **That's the kind of person we have the opportunity to send to Congress**.
Sam knows what it's like to have your future and your life shaped by money, or by not having enough of it. After college, Sam dreamed of going to law school. But he looked at his student loan debt, and realized that he couldn't afford it.
That’s the same story I experienced. I wanted to go to medical school, but my dad had passed away, my mom was a single mom, and I knew my family couldn’t afford for me to spend years out of the workforce.
**This is what it means to be a working person, not only in Montana, but everywhere**. And this is about all of us, together.
The question before us isn't whether we should send another politician to Washington. It's whether we send someone who will fight.
A working person who understands real life, who doesn’t need to have it explained to them, but has actually had to make the dollars and cents work at the end of the month.
It is that proximity that gives us the urgency to change things, not “one day,” but _now_. And **Sam Forstag has been running toward that his whole life**.
Sam is asking for the chance to take that fight to Washington. And I think he should have it.
Sam is going to run towards the fire in D.C. the same way he has run towards the fire at home. **But he cannot do it alone**.
[Will you split a $5 contribution today — $2.50 each for Sam’s team and mine — so that we can elect a true brawler for the working class to Congress on June 2nd? Every dollar fuels our campaigns for progress.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260529-forstag.9ts18M&refcode=em20260529-11552-P_FND_SPL_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=11552%2E2526796%2ET1hpP3)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260529-forstag.9ts18M&refcode=em20260529-11552-P_FND_SPL_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=40&akid=11552%2E2526796%2ET1hpP3)**
We’re fighting for our kids, we’re fighting for our houses, we’re fighting for our water, we’re fighting to have a government that belongs to us now.
And we do that by electing Sam Forstag to Congress.
Whether or not you can give today, **thank you for standing with us**.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

That means something: when something is burning, Sam runs toward that fire. That’s who he is. That's the kind of person we have the opportunity to send to Congress. Sam knows what it's like to have your future and your life shaped by money, or by not having enough of it. After college, Sam dreamed of going to law school. But he looked at his student loan debt, and realized that he couldn't afford it. That’s the same story I experienced. I wanted to go to medical school, but my dad had passed away, my mom was a single mom, and I knew my family couldn’t afford for me to spend years out of the workforce. This is what it means to be a working person, not only in Montana, but everywhere. And this is about all of us, together. The question before us isn't whether we should send another politician to Washington. It's whether we send someone who will fight. A working person who understands real life, who doesn’t need to have it explained to them, but has actually had to make the dollars and cents work at the end of the month. It is that proximity that gives us the urgency to change things, not “one day,” but now. And Sam Forstag has been running toward that his whole life. Sam is asking for the chance to take that fight to Washington. And I think he should have it. Sam is going to run towards the fire in D.C. the same way he has run towards the fire at home. But he cannot do it alone. We’re fighting for our kids, we’re fighting for our houses, we’re fighting for our water, we’re fighting to have a government that belongs to us now. And we do that by electing Sam Forstag to Congress. Whether or not you can give today, thank you for standing with us. In solidarity, Alexandria | ---|--- | | | ---|---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

Thanks to Donald Trump, prices on everyday goods are skyrocketing for Marylanders. Families are deciding between groceries and gas, yet Republicans remain silent. **It’s unacceptable.**
But right now, let me tell you about the things we’re doing to create a little bit more breathing room for Maryland:
✅ We banned surveillance-based dynamic pricing, so the price you see on the shelf at the grocery store is the same price you’ll pay at the register.
✅ We increased income for over 160,000 Marylanders by raising the minimum wage to $15/hour.
✅ We are fighting to hold energy companies accountable, invest in clean energy expansions and lower energy costs.
✅ We executed a robust housing agenda that turns renters into homeowners, increasing housing supply.
As long as I am Maryland's governor, **I will never let Trump, or any of his allies, run roughshod over our state with their dangerous agenda.**

clean_body: Peter, this email matters. I don’t need to tell you that our wallets are being stretched thin. Thanks to Donald Trump, prices on everyday goods are skyrocketing for Marylanders. Families are deciding between groceries and gas, yet Republicans remain silent. It’s unacceptable. But right now, let me tell you about the things we’re doing to create a little bit more breathing room for Maryland: ✅ We banned surveillance-based dynamic pricing, so the price you see on the shelf at the grocery store is the same price you’ll pay at the register. ✅ We increased income for over 160,000 Marylanders by raising the minimum wage to $15/hour. ✅ We are fighting to hold energy companies accountable, invest in clean energy expansions and lower energy costs. ✅ We executed a robust housing agenda that turns renters into homeowners, increasing housing supply. As long as I am Maryland's governor, I will never let Trump, or any of his allies, run roughshod over our state with their dangerous agenda. Elevate, Wes

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Dear friend,
This picture really doesn’t reflect it well, but I LOVED climbing trees as a kid!
The little girl in this tree had no idea what the future would hold, but she was growing up in a family and in a community that would shape her values for life.
My family and this community taught me about hard work, resilience, and caring for those around you. They shaped me into who I am. I want our children and future generations to grow up with those same foundations, and with even more opportunities than we had.
As the school year ends and summer begins, families across our community are preparing for more than camps and vacations.
For many kids, school is where they find steady meals, safe spaces, and trusted adults. When those doors close for summer, too many families will be trying to fill those gaps.
At a time when affordable healthcare and food assistance are under attack, the stakes for working families couldn’t be higher. And this race will be CRITICAL to winning back the U.S. House of Representatives and stopping Trump’s attacks on the safety nets that protect families.
It’s almost the end of the month, and that means the support we raise now helps us keep fighting for families, protect essential programs, and make sure no child is left behind when school lets out.
Will you chip in now to help us hit our May end-of-month goal so we can keep organizing, reaching voters, and fighting for healthcare and food security for families? By now, you have likely heard the deeply concerning news about the massive mail-in ballot breakdown right here in Maryland.

| Peter,

By now, you have likely heard the deeply concerning news about the massive mail-in ballot breakdown right here in Maryland.

Due to a major printing error by a third-party mailing vendor, the State Board of Elections discovered that an unknown number of primary voters were sent ballots for the wrong political party. Because there was no way to pinpoint exactly who received an incorrect ballot, election officials had to make an unprecedented call: **reprinting and reissuing mail-in ballots to more than 565,000 Marylanders.**

This vendor blunder is incredibly frustrating. It creates unnecessary confusion and threatens to undermine voter confidence at a time when participation is absolutely critical. But we cannot let logistical failures silence our voices. We need to push through the confusion and make sure our community votes.

_If you requested a mail-in ballot, here is exactly what you need to know right now to ensure your vote is counted:_
* **Do not cast your original ballot:** If you received an early ballot in the mail, please do not fill it out or return it. The state will not count those original ballots.
* **Look for your replacement:** A completely new ballot packet has been rushed to your mailbox. If you haven't received it yet, it should be arriving any day now. The new envelope will be clearly marked "REPLACEMENT BALLOT." This is the only ballot you should fill out and return.
* **Returning your replacement:** Once you fill out the replacement ballot, it can be mailed, dropped in an official ballot drop box location, or taken directly to a polling place or Early Voting Center by 8:00 pm on Election Day.

For the latest updates, ballot box locations, and further details, please visit the website of the Maryland State Board of Elections.

Our campaign team is already hitting the phones and leaving these instructions for voters across the community, but we need your help to spread the word. **Please share these steps with your family, friends, and neighbors who plan to vote by mail.**

Thank you for your resilience, your dedication to our community, and your continued hard work to help us win this race. Let's make sure every single voice is heard.

Sincerely,

John Block
_Campaign Manager_

Washington is full of politicians who love to talk about abstract theories but have absolutely no idea how a local community actually functions. Before asking for your vote for Congress, I put in the work on the Nashville Metro Council representing District 4. **It 's simple, but think about how important that is for our government.**
On the council, you can't hide behind partisan talking points. When a neighbor calls about a zoning issue, a broken transit route, or a rising rent bill, you have to show up and find solutions. Serving on the Budget and Finance committee taught me exactly how to look at a balance sheet and figure out who is being taken care of and who is being left behind.
I'm running for Congress to scale up the fight for affordable living, fair wages, and honest governance. But unlike the politicians backed by billionaire super PACs, this campaign is funded by real people giving what they can.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d6867baa-de57-446f-8d66-936cf27d53a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**[If you believe Washington needs more local public servants and fewer corporate puppets, please consider donating $25 to our campaign today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/848088a2-7dd1-4e2f-9844-3a6b4f3ee836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ ☑️ DONATE ☑️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/848088a2-7dd1-4e2f-9844-3a6b4f3ee836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Right now, the federal government's budget leaves working families behind every single day. The same corporate interests I've pushed back against at the local level are writing the rules in Washington**. I want to bring that exact same municipal accountability to the federal level.**
Let's bring the fight to them, because they will never bring it to us.

Peter,

Today I’m in Columbia, South Carolina — and I want to tell you why it matters.

I'll be headlining the South Carolina Democratic Party's Blue Palmetto Dinner at the State Fairgrounds. It's one of the most important Democratic events in the country and I’m honored to have this opportunity.

South Carolina Democrats are building something real. They're organizing in every county, recruiting candidates up and down the ballot, and laying the groundwork for 2026 with the seriousness and discipline that wins elections.

I believe we have to compete everywhere. Not just in the states we're supposed to win. Not just in the “easy” places. Everywhere.

I've spent the last six years governing a state that Donald Trump won by 31 points in 2024. And I've learned that when you show up, listen, and lead with people's lives instead of politics, you can win in places that nobody expected. You can deliver healthcare to people who never had it. You can bring jobs to communities that felt forgotten. You can earn trust that lasts.

South Carolina deserves that kind of fight. And so does every state where Democrats have been told not to bother.

The work I'm doing is about building that kind of map, one where we don't concede a single state before the campaign even starts. And events like tonight are how we build the infrastructure, the energy, and the resources to do it.
