**[One Colorado built the GSA network. Now it’s backing the campaign against Initiatives 109 and 110.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **A "grassroots" committee funded almost entirely by outside groups:** Families Not Politics raised nearly $320,000 in three months to defeat Initiatives 109 and 110, with ~90% coming from Cobalt Advocates (formerly NARAL), Planned Parenthood, a Portland PAC, and One Colorado Education Fund — none from Colorado parents' organizations.
* **One Colorado built the GSA network that started this fight and is now leading the opposition:** One Colorado runs the statewide GSA network named by Poudre School District as a guiding resource after a 2021 incident where Erin Lee's 6th-grade daughter was secretly invited to a GSA meeting, told her parents weren't safe, and came home identifying as transgender — spurring the years-long fight that produced Initiatives 109 and 110.
* **The opposition is misrepresenting both initiatives:** Families Not Politics claims Initiative 109 would subject girls to "invasive gender inspections" and Initiative 110 could block cancer surgeries — but the final text of 109 contains no inspection process, and 110 explicitly excludes treatment for physical abnormalities, meaning cancer surgery is not affected. Erin Lee will speak at RMV's Freedom Fest on June 26.

* **Unaffiliated voters now outnumber both parties combined in Colorado:** Out of 3,996,931 registered voters, Democrats hold 24.86%, Republicans 22.47%, and unaffiliated/other voters 52.68% — a bloc that guest commentator and 50-year Colorado resident Russ Minary argues both parties are failing by prioritizing ideology and infighting over the concerns of average taxpayers.
* **Conservatives are losing because they campaign against people instead of for ideas:** Minary argues the Colorado GOP has failed to articulate a clear platform for two to three decades, and that the path to winning unaffiliated voters is campaigning on specific, positive commitments — pointing to Trump's 20 Core Promises in 2024 as the model that works.
* **Nine principles borrowed from business and sports could turn it around:** Minary lays out a nine-point framework — define your purpose, serve your constituents, set accountability standards, manage by results — arguing the same discipline that wins championships can win Colorado back for conservatives if leaders demand it of themselves first.

The evening features a BBQ dinner, live music from the Curtis Grimes Band , remarks from Colorado District Attorneys George Brauchler and Michael Allen , and a keynote address from television icon Duane "Dog the Bounty Hunter" Chapman. Attendees will also hear from Pastor Lorenzo Sewell, who delivered the invocation at the Presidential Inauguration. One Colorado built the GSA network that started this fight and is now leading the opposition: One Colorado runs the statewide GSA network named by Poudre School District as a guiding resource after a 2021 incident where Erin Lee's 6th-grade daughter was secretly invited to a GSA meeting, told her parents weren't safe, and came home identifying as transgender — spurring the years-long fight that produced Initiatives 109 and 110. Thanks to him, schools have gone underfunded, healthcare has stayed out of reach, costs have climbed higher and higher, and families have been squeezed from every direction. And while Texans struggle, Abbott keeps choosing the same people he always has: wealthy donors, powerful and corrupt insiders, anti-choice extremists, and Donald Trump. Texas is getting national attention because Republicans are being forced to admit that the Lone Star state is more competitive than they want voters to believe. body:

Yesterday, I took to the debate stage with my fellow Democratic attorney general candidates, and truthfully, I’m more fired up than ever about this fight.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2-debatevideo?refcode=x_260529_debate_eom1_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2-debatevideo?refcode=x_260529_debate_eom1_act]
In case you missed it, you can watch the livestream here. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2-debatevideo?refcode=x_260529_debate_eom1_act]
WATCH DEBATE HERE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2-debatevideo?refcode=x_260529_debate_eom1_act]
Yesterday was about more than just political mudslinging. It was about who is actually ready to stand up to the powerful interests making life harder for working people across Colorado.
While career politicians talk, real Coloradans are struggling to afford basic necessities, and fewer can trust that the system will ever work for them.
As I said on the stage yesterday, corporations and billionaires are ripping us off and getting away with it. Working people are seeing prices go up while the wealthy and powerful continue to rig the system in their favor. Meanwhile, giant corporations pollute our planet, invade our privacy, and put profits ahead of people every chance they get.
I got into this race because I know there’s a better way. I’m the only candidate who has spent my career taking on corporate monopolies, landlords, and special interests that think the rules don’t apply to them. And tonight, I made it clear in front of all of Colorado: we need an attorney general who isn’t afraid to fight for the many, not the money.
That’s the leadership Colorado deserves.
And after tonight , it’s clear: People are hungry for bold leadership and someone willing to take on the toughest fights head-on.
The reality is that tonight’s debate will bring more attention, more scrutiny, and, yes, more attacks from the powerful interests that do not want someone like me in the attorney general’s office.
So I’m asking: can you chip in tonight before our end-of-month deadline to help us keep this momentum growing? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2-debatevideo?refcode=x_260529_debate_eom1_act]

body:
Peter,

Here's the reality: Democrats have what it takes to win back the House majority this November.

The main super PAC for Senate Republicans unveiled a plan to flood $342 MILLION into eight battleground races. The guy in charge even said he is “100 percent confident” this investment will save the GOP majority. So if we plan on proving him wrong, we have to get back on track to reach our $50,000 end-of-month goal immediately. = | | = Look, we've all known for years that the 2026 map heavily favors the GOP. And this fall, Democrats must flip at least four seats to take back the majority. We also know Trump's brand is growing more toxic by the hour – and now that experts at The Cook Political Report have shifted race ratings LEFT in four states Trump carried last cycle, we’re on the cusp of real momentum. But between a tough map and truly massive Republican investments, we have zero room for error on a single goal between now and Election Day. body:
Trump wants to cut Social Security checks for 400,000 disabled Americans.
# [](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/51612?refcode=jtk554-fr-nd-header&t=1&akid=10786%2E434096%2Epx89hO)
| | |
---
**Derek, Trump wants to cut Social Security checks for 400,000 disabled Americans. Just like that.**
We're talking about people already living in poverty – families surviving on $17,000 a year. And the GOP wants to take MORE from them.
Right now, the maximum Social Security benefit is $994 a month. That's already less than the poverty line. Under this new rule, that drops to $663.
They're calling these cuts "program integrity."
_That's not integrity. It's just wrong._ 🤬
**Their goal is simple: break Social Security, run it dry, and sell it for scrap. All so the ultrawealthy can keep their tax breaks.**
Not on my watch.
I'm fighting in the Senate to protect Social Security – for seniors, for disabled Americans, for every working family that has paid into this system their entire lives – but I can't do it alone. **I need you with me.**

We have four days to power Randy Villegas to victory — it’s a win we can’t afford to fumble.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260529-1&t=1&akid=3539%2E587540%2E-F_yjQ)
This is it, Peter.
**Four days until Randy Villegas’ primary.** These next few days could determine whether the Central Valley finally gets a fighter for working people or the establishment keeps calling the shots.
**June 2** is the moment it all comes down to — _and this is a win we can’t afford to fumble._
I’ll tell you more, but first, **[will you split a $5 donation between Randy and Leaders We Deserve?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260529_1_randy.zuyvtt&refcode=em20260529-3539&amount=5&t=2&akid=3539%2E587540%2E-F_yjQ)**

I’ve been to the Central Valley. I’ve talked to the student volunteers knocking doors with Randy, and I’ve felt the genuine hope and excitement he’s inspiring in thousands of young people who desperately want Democratic leaders they can actually trust to fight for them.
That kind of energy doesn’t come from another cookie cutter candidate propped up by the Party machine. It comes from a fearless, people-powered leader who actually means what he says.
And it’s exactly how we change the face of power in this Party — one bold leader and one fired up volunteer at a time. The establishment knows this. It’s why they’ve thrown _everything_ they’ve got at this race.
AIPAC and their affiliate PACs are backing Randy’s opponent — flooding the field with $2.8 million dollars in the final 2 weeks to push through a candidate who will be loyal to them, not the voters. And even with the weight of the DCCC and AIPAC behind his opponent, every metric shows that Randy is the stronger candidate in this race and the best shot Democrats have at flipping this seat and the House in November.
If Randy wins on Tuesday, it will prove that people-powered candidates _can_ beat the machine. And it will send a message that this movement is destined to grow and _nothing_ will deter us. And we’ll make history — **Randy would be the first Latino representative CA-22 has ever sent to Congress.**
We cannot allow the same greedy, corrupt politics that have failed this district for decades to continue. Winning on Tuesday is going to take one final push to make sure every voter in the Central Valley has an opportunity to connect with Randy and his message before **June 2** — and we’re counting on your support to get him over the finish line.
**[Will you split a $5 donation between Randy and Leaders We Deserve to power him to victory on Tuesday?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260529_1_randy.zuyvtt&refcode=em20260529-3539&amount=5&t=4&akid=3539%2E587540%2E-F_yjQ)**

David Hogg

## Airman Reunites With Military Dog
Senior Airman Alex Jones met a military working dog named Max while stationed in Korea in 2020. The two weren't assigned to work together, but they [formed a close bond](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ypDAQhJ8GMlFCSPwECi4h20svpGZhBDpLGmqQV963d-FXcNxdXf19_x7LA3zwaf8LEa3b3ZIdLQnLFTBn5CXC10oRr4MiMu3IF2P-5HQtSqpeSCPUtGzgw3vR9WYdosKuRtsOo5SjkVNfH3aUUzv2etKw9aoz4LZpNMogOG36px5qb-81adSkpNRGN21rnpPq2vW54tgOfaUlbj4TN__Jp3ygC296ITcrxTrYI-fzqro_lZorNZdSmhMz7HjHlZpPKJcgJwqwgCQwUvaUIIibaqXo0y58Eok4H2IFpuATCEcsDmQS0Qefgd-iEH_c3Y32Ss012-0sPgR_9UOl5R7Bh59D-dcmX1Z9BwAA___Hroxj), and Alex spent years waiting for the day Max would retire from service. That day finally came. name: Rob Bonta
subject: They collected personal data from millions, then lied about a data breach. We’re suing.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ROB BONTA FOR CALIFORNIA ATTORNEY GENERAL 2026 FPPC ID #145642
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Friends, California is filing a lawsuit against Chrome Holding Co. — formerly known as 23andMe — for violating multiple state laws and utterly failing consumers in a dangerous and deeply disturbing way.
In 2023, after years of collecting sensitive, private information from millions of people — including mine, by the way, and perhaps yours, too — 23andMe’s failure to implement basic security measures led to a catastrophic data breach. Then they lied about it.
We’re talking about personal information like genetic risk factors, biological relatives, ancestry, and ethnicity.
News of the breach first came to light after the data of one million consumers was offered for sale on the dark web, specifically advertised as belonging to Asian American and Pacific Islander and Jewish users. This happened during a period of rising anti-AAPI and antisemitic hate and violence, making an already horrifying breach even more disturbing.
Your data belongs to you, and only you, not to a company and certainly not to a bad actor who stole or illegally bought it on the dark web.
We’re suing today because California will always stand up to corporations that play fast and loose with our data — corporations that think compliance is optional, and consumers exist to be exploited.
This is exactly the work your support makes possible. If you want to keep it going, please contribute to my re-election campaign so we can continue the fight to secure justice and accountability for all. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

The 2023 data breach affected nearly 7 million customers across the country, including more than 800,000 Californians.
23andMe knew their customers’ data was at risk. Not only were their security measures woefully deficient, they repeatedly misled consumers about the security of their products to induce more people to use their services!
In the aftermath of the breach, the company was simultaneously engaging in ransom negotiations with the threat actor while actively misleading consumers and downplaying the severity of the breach . They then agreed to the ransom demands and paid $400,000 in cryptocurrency for the threat actor to destroy the stolen data.
They tried to hide both the severity of the breach and their own responsibility for it. They violated a state data security law, consumer privacy law, and false advertising law, among others.
Consumers deserve accountability, and with today’s lawsuit, we’re asking the court to deliver it.
As Attorney General, I am committed to protecting Californians from any and all bad actors who put your rights at risk. We’re fighting back — and we’re winning.

body:
There’s a new plan to attack Social Security. This Court won’t do anything to stop it. | |
---
Peter, **Congressional Republicans and their Wall Street billionaire backers never stop trying to cut our Social Security benefits. Their newest plan is a wolf in sheep’s clothing.** They’re proposing to cap Social Security benefits at $100,000 per household. Sounds like a good way to stop millionaires from dipping into the pot, right? Wrong. First of all, millionaires don’t depend on Social Security for retirement in the first place. This won’t affect them in the slightest. But more importantly, anyone who lives in or near New York City, Boston, San Francisco, or any of America’s other major cities knows $50,000 a year isn’t enough to get by. **It’s a sneaky, billionaire-backed way to cut benefits for regular, working people.** **For nearly a century, millionaires and billionaires have gotten away with not paying in to Social Security on their full income.** As more everyday Americans wake up that the choice is between cutting middle class benefits or taxing the rich, Wall Street billionaires are trying to redirect our focus to this new cap on benefits instead. **But the same forces who have been trying to dismantle Social Security for nearly a century are behind perverting the Supreme Court. Their goal is a country that works for the ultra-rich and leaves the rest of us behind.** **[We need Congress to step up and kill this plan before it can begin. Tell them not to cut our benefits, but to expand Social Security by taxing the rich who are profiting off our rigged economy. Write to your representative and senators now >>](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3__SP4NT9ipRN1xMeMP0xGZR3yJaY_Qc_oIqTYE5fFD9_o-ru6iJGtWV-yeJ-4ZanqFDklh8I2T9RWZMzM92MS1SOqVOs9zcnu3CFC6dVqLkI9l4h_dp54LiJ5sxyOJIHRci1F3M5sB88nYBiNl9rqMzZMMn_wFV3ENBQustJFI6o4sK0tz2U8ncQwbSQbfSN-KfaRHZSW1zmuYCSbArQmTjoIi-1cN6Sq0aPhAxf2SbTlOWv-byOSSmKBLwXtTvCQJ2a_AWcvtLJOCHnlKM5n1vzFgJPE9PdPnCMdf4ArB8iB6SD7vxvRU16jWn33UAv0wi9Gy3NKxoswk7vfvRsLkxmSoovwuPolTm5Cj6N5ocgUrnaeiAbca0nvcJa5OFv5jX-wF_jcEJsjxvY1MOZIq/4r1/RN8O7KXvTsWnLeT4lrZUIQ/h0/h001.udqxdFjArSLXJAUYPJKgj1c9S1l75nV81y4vmzM-0ZA)** [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3__SP4NT9ipRN1xMeMP0xGZR3yJaY_Qc_oIqTYE5fFD9_o-ru6iJGtWV-yeJ-4ZanqFDklh8I2T9RWZMzM92MS1SOqVOs9zcnu3CFC6dVqLkI9l4h_dp54LiJ5sxyOJIHRci1F3M5sB88nYBiNl9rqMzZMMn_wFV3ENBQustJFI6o4sK0tz2U8ncQwbSQbfSN-KfaRHZSW1zmuYCSbArQmT_MGuzooOHn7MTEyYcv14cUPrIinnWpT9WvrwIROA8C-EzFXfXN6weueu4fN2j4LfjAqyIvltzbWyKQ7taoy2ImOxDFBd7BAid6S0cDgNZ8Gx5mHLq-9jLyvEYXQ9jpchToXoQq5kNNs7xHAkdYSeYrrsNJugfhH8cBL3bPmjmh41prI88VYSIDScLtd3990g/4r1/RN8O7KXvTsWnLeT4lrZUIQ/h1/h001.Pk4xuFy4sc_4TSqdXS4Rx4a8f2WAEoCWt5UKXYHR3jo) Social Security is one of the most important, popular promises our American democracy is built on. If you work hard your whole life, you’ll be able to retire comfortably. That was what President Franklin D. Roosevelt intended when he proposed our Social Security system nearly a century ago. At the time, a plutocrat-captured Supreme Court stood against many of his New Deal programs. Instead of capitulating to the “economic royalists” of his day, FDR made his case to the American people that the Supreme Court was the problem, and needed reform. **He worked to add new members to the Supreme Court when it was clear the current members wouldn’t represent the will of the people.** The plan, he said, would “save the Constitution from the Court and the Court from itself.” He called the justices out for their attitude that “something in the Constitution has compelled them regretfully to thwart the will of the people.” Ultimately, the Supreme Court started listening to the people, and FDR’s plans made America a more democratic and more equal country. **Unfortunately, too many of us have forgotten the lessons of FDR.** Now, we have a Court that’s put billionaire wealth over our families. They won’t help seniors afford healthcare and housing by expanding Social Security—they’ll join the extremist effort to gut it. **[We can’t let the wealthy and powerful turn the promise of Social Security into a flat, poverty-level benefit. Friend,

Real leadership isn't measured by how much noise you make on a cable news set, how many likes you get on a post, or how flashy your speeches are. It is measured by the steady, day-to-day commitments required to deliver actual results for the people you represent.

For years, I’ve focused on doing that heavy lifting; first in Annapolis, and now representing the Third District in Washington. We are focused on the issues that actually matter to Maryland families — from tackling the affordability crisis to protecting the Chesapeake Bay to expanding access to quality health care.

But as the calendar turns to June, the scale of this race shifts.

We are officially entering the final 25-day stretch before the primary. The decisions awaiting us in Washington are far too consequential to leave to chance, and we cannot afford to look back in mid-June, wondering whether we did enough to get our message in front of voters.

When the calendar flips on Monday, the partisan theatrics from our opponents are only going to get louder. To ensure we have the baseline tools in place to tune out the noise and stay focused on our neighborhoods, our team is working to get as many grassroots partners on board as possible before June 1st.

If you are ready to prioritize the tangible needs of Maryland families over performance art, I hope you’ll consider partnering with us today. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Hi friends — this is an end-of-month fundraising email. I wanted to tell you right off the bat so you can delete it if you’d prefer! I understand it may not be possible to give right now (or you may just be sick of being asked).
So no hard feelings if this is the last sentence you read before clicking that trash icon.
If you’ve stuck around, I’m glad, because this is so important to talk about:
Right now, the stakes of everything feel so high. I remember in 2016, working on Hillary Clinton’s campaign, some people said our fears about a Donald Trump presidency were unfounded. That we were “overreacting.” That we were hysterical .
A decade later, we watch videos of families being ripped apart, innocent children being detained and mistreated in custody, and Americans being murdered by masked ICE and Border Patrol agents in our communities.
https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/2026/05/16/she-was-deported-without-her-toddler-then-ice-blamed-her-his-murder/ [https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/2026/05/16/she-was-deported-without-her-toddler-then-ice-blamed-her-his-murder/]
We watch millions of Americans struggle to afford gas, groceries, child care, and housing — while the GOP and Trump push to gut Medicaid and health care to pay for a $1 billion ballroom and an illegal, unnecessary, and reckless war.
https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/05/politics/ballroom-security-ice-cbp-senate-gop-bill [https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/05/politics/ballroom-security-ice-cbp-senate-gop-bill]
We see children, people with disabilities, and seniors going hungry because Republicans just slashed food assistance at a moment when everything is already unaffordable.
https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-food-stamp-cuts-children-arizona-hungry-big-beautiful-bill-rcna343922 [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-food-stamp-cuts-children-arizona-hungry-big-beautiful-bill-rcna343922]
We watch Donald Trump claim to care about “waste, fraud, abuse” — and then turn around and create a $1.8 billion slush fund with taxpayer dollars for insurrectionists.
https://www.wsj.com/us-news/law/trump-irs-lawsuit-settlement-fund-c3edaf3f [https://www.wsj.com/us-news/law/trump-irs-lawsuit-settlement-fund-c3edaf3f]
We see states trying to criminalize people seeking health care — even introducing bills to allow *deadly force* for those seeking an abortion.
https://www.wcnc.com/article/news/politics/north-carolina-politics/north-carolina-bill-would-authorize-deadly-force-for-women-seeking-abortions/275-353d54a3-9231-4341-ae44-a127546db76f [https://www.wcnc.com/article/news/politics/north-carolina-politics/north-carolina-bill-would-authorize-deadly-force-for-women-seeking-abortions/275-353d54a3-9231-4341-ae44-a127546db76f]
All of that barely scratches the surface of this administration’s corruption and cruelty — and we’re not even halfway through year two.
We all know that we have to keep taking action to defend our democracy, but it’s daunting and draining.
So here’s my promise to you: I will do every single thing in my power to fight for you and your rights. I will use every legislative tool, partner with our allies in the judicial system and out in the community, and push hard to protect our values and our freedoms.
But I’ll also tell you this — we’ll be a lot more successful in that work if we can claw back the GOP trifecta in Washington, and this November we have our chance.
My team and I are finalizing our plans for the midterms: winning re-election in CA-51, supporting my House colleagues in tough races, and boosting strong Democratic challengers in key battleground districts.
Will you help? We’re trying to raise $4,310 more online before the end of May to keep our plans on track — anything you can give towards that goal will make a difference.
Click here or on the buttons below to contribute before we close the books on our May fundraising. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]

—Sara

We need you to take a look at this.
| Peter,
Actions speak louder than words.
This weekend, we witnessed a tale of two campaigns. It showed exactly where each candidate's priorities lie.
While Graham Platner decided to use Memorial Day to host a political rally with Bernie Sanders, Senator Susan Collins was where she always is: standing respectfully with Mainers.
Following a heartbreaking tragedy, Susan attended the funeral of a fallen Maine firefighter to mourn with the community. Also, she joined a local parade to honor the brave heroes who laid down their lives to protect our country.
No grandstanding. No political stunts. Just showing up for Maine.
This is a glaring example of how each candidate operates.
Platner puts politics first. Susan Collins puts Maine first.
We cannot let out-of-touch politicians turn every sacred day into a partisan rally. We need to keep a true champion for Maine in the Senate, but Chuck Schumer and his allies are doing everything they can to buy this seat.
We need your help to fight back.
[Can we count on you to stand up for Susan Collins today?](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=4375b3e4100746aca727ac52d5447a4e&_e=qFuNJQ3x5gpLDLr1bma7pNYdlp-0oUocwIV_BDOsZNFMFQjDST9v-tVD-dwaMzeSH2XN4NY03j5-MUw4D1scIdCHqHbrj7SGjK9mWOzkage14mhB1UHkJpBrNxOmzo5NpcF0CNVNWNZU0xTqoZ7lQQKsT-RgmgNY6nVk2YubcTW_UrvFCO0pOjChQ1h9G53mfLd1x5vBqSHYnJnl1SC5fZYMxxpeGwAtV8KEI2ayhHhnIZZmIIhZ0QEPGzX_sNRmfgZuykyG9ysQ7sah_tMgrd3Mfi3ygGnURSAuHcC1kAc9wTNuEeBjOFUynPwTTmR_nNZ8n7ZUx1udxZbzgt_oP7QCXiifOznkTrQMle5K-sbfawr8WVDpZGHAkjk4uvHjc4D5xtdTYlHCSY7Jp9iYQEUlMQ2zSGWtxYLwUUv7FeFPkV4usW40WiK1h8fJDJWIb0lgeQspXHEFl7K0OQrVLvSyx4O_KwZZF99WjBN07-Y4ML4Yt5IlRYkgIhYIXxHHzi6hgu_9ohWboRJoDMqLeixGEy5XG1HqjGKlB0nvNiPio64Jh-XAftnFDuH6XAT7d-tuVZ4dMv_XrnUzUsxxhZra7TYQ1tR9jiAXNPkJ1UgwwyXZi3J9HOk7qKaJUeAt5hMytqjqoI0O0jC1rVca-CqTBKhyzWWGxfpwKIpo8-wE77b01dkPh6cCxwDgSnLYQF094SRHuccIitsIbPqIuVOXzgUgRgRvZk-d20UPkuvjAo1mrkLpjDWic5oTx3ew1rU0b4SfeVZWA6UlSrxH3x1TMZu2Eky4iSCVyjWdA8Mh9qYKA5ULG3-gXckcJ52CmtUbHcyi4t3c_imvc-kc0uq71ZliKEJoZk5nFuL1Ve-xDRwJXk4sfSv5i5_Q3mQeDxv3NtKC3z4uK5QcS6wnIg%3D%3D)

clean_body: We need you to take a look at this. | Peter, Actions speak louder than words. This weekend, we witnessed a tale of two campaigns. It showed exactly where each candidate's priorities lie. While Graham Platner decided to use Memorial Day to host a political rally with Bernie Sanders, Senator Susan Collins was where she always is: standing respectfully with Mainers. Following a heartbreaking tragedy, Susan attended the funeral of a fallen Maine firefighter to mourn with the community. Also, she joined a local parade to honor the brave heroes who laid down their lives to protect our country. No grandstanding. No political stunts. Just showing up for Maine. This is a glaring example of how each candidate operates. Platner puts politics first. Susan Collins puts Maine first. We cannot let out-of-touch politicians turn every sacred day into a partisan rally. We need to keep a true champion for Maine in the Senate, but Chuck Schumer and his allies are doing everything they can to buy this seat. We need your help to fight back. | | | Right now, our opponents and outside special interest groups are pouring money into Maine, flooding the digital airwaves with attacks designed to distort Susan's record of independent leadership. They think they can use out-of-state money to buy up every ad slot to drown out common sense. We cannot let them have the last word. The Radical Left has an endless supply of dark money that they are using to drown out the truth. We need your help, now more than ever, to keep our ads on the digital airwaves. Today we buried my mom, and I want to take a minute to share with you just a few of the things she taught me.
She taught me how to drive stick.
She taught me to be fiercely competitive in sports and the occasional card game. Definitely not Wordle.
She taught me to only eat strawberries that are grown here in Pennsylvania, and only eat them in season.
She taught me that homemade jelly is the only conceivable option. And once you ate hers, you could never even think about a jar of Smucker's from the store.
She taught me to love state parks, and to pick up trash when you see it.
She taught me to love music. She taught me the Methodist hymnal. She paid for piano lessons for years, with poor results. She taught me that, regardless of how I felt about it, being in the high school marching band was not optional.
She taught me that you show up for family - whether it's the reunion every July, or Fastnacht Day before Lent.
She taught me that being Pennsylvania Dutch meant you were kind, hardworking, humble, and never said no to a soft pretzel.
She taught me to persevere - even when it got hard. Even when she got Parkinson's.
She taught me not to be afraid of death.
**But ask any of my family to try and boil it all down into a bumper sticker, and we will all tell you: Mom taught us to seldom repress a generous impulse.**
**Seldom repress a generous impulse.**
And Mom almost never did.
She was an outrageous tipper, which is why she was beloved at Roma Pizza in Pottsville, where you would often find her on Friday evenings.
She made an effort to be kind to everyone she met - whether she worked with you, went to church with you, or just saw you walking in Baber Cemetery, which she did twice a day, every day of our lives, weather and her health permitting.
But it was more than that. Karen Wallace went above and beyond.
Were you in need of a car? She would give you a ride, or pick you up if you were hitchhiking. That made for one fun Thanksgiving.
She would lend you her hulking van, which somehow still passes inspection. Or show up with it and help you move. She would work it out with our dad to gift you one of their cars.
Were you in need of housing? She would send you money. Or open up her house and let you move in.
Were you in need of a kidney? She had two - one to spare. Ask and it was yours.
These are all true stories. Mom was extraordinary in her generosity.
American politics doesn't feel like a place for generous impulses. But my mom taught me that caring for your community, like marching band in high school, wasn't optional. And when you feel the impulse to do something to help others - seldom repress it.
Mom is gone. But her legacy isn't. So, we march on.
Thank you for allowing me to share her memory with you here.

Peter,
Donating to Voto Latino is one of the most direct ways to grow Latino voter participation in the elections that will decide our future.
[**If you’re ready to help power our voter registration work right now, chip in $3 or any amount today.**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260529-2-ak.qJAl_f&amount=3&refcode=em20260529-184&t=1&akid=184%2E1366028%2EYHw1ca)
Here are three powerful reasons why you should make an investment in Voto Latino today:
**1\. We know how to register Latino voters.**
**We’ve helped more than 9.5 million people navigate the voting process** , from registering and checking status to finding polling locations and making a plan to vote. Registering voters is how we fight back against Trump and his allies’ anti-voter stunts, because the more of us who are on the rolls and ready to vote, the harder it is for them to silence us.

**2\. Our work has a proven track record.**
**Since 2004, we’ve registered nearly 2 million voters**. In 2020 alone, we registered more than**650,000 voters** , and **82% of those voters turned out.** Since 2012, we’ve registered **334,484 voters in battleground states** where elections are often decided by razor-thin margins.
**3\. The work is urgent, and the gap is still real.**
Millions of eligible Latino voters are still unregistered. With the midterms just**six months away and _even less time_ before voter registration deadlines**, closing that gap now means more people informed, registered, and ready to show up when it counts. Because we know that in race after race this November, Latinos _will_ be the margin of victory.
Right now, we set a goal of raising $10,000 by Sunday, May 31st, so we can keep doing what we do best — organizing and reaching voters. **So if these three reasons convinced you:**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

# [For the people I love](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=199635276&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5NjM1Mjc2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODAwODg3NzEsImV4cCI6MTc4MjY4MDc3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.dcEz_RC6IM6sWJEGYxEEpyYlAKntX8FD4g0SJ6lg38c)
### My Michigan Hope Agenda is my promise to speak up, fight, and deliver for all Michiganders.
May 29
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..-QA6CJQJxxxsjrTQifl7vtqrto7HbmiUPohr1Q5xbhc?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/for-the-people-i-love?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Recently, I had a chance to spend some time with Michiganders at Memorial Day events, church services, and a local charity event in Detroit.
And I want to tell you what I keep hearing:_Too many folks feel left behind right now._
Michiganders are stretched. Many are flat-out exhausted. They've been working their whole lives and somehow it's harder than ever to get by.
But when I look around Michigan, I see a state of fighters. They are still working, still raising their kids, still showing up for their neighbors, still believing that this place is worth fighting for. They are not asking for a handout. They are asking for a government that works for them in simple ways. A government that makes their lives just a little easier.
That is what I am running to build.
**The MI Hope Agenda is my love letter to Michiganders - especially to the Black and brown communities in our state that have been overlooked, underfunded, and asked to wait for too long.**
I have spent a lot of time on Substack lately telling you about the corruption of Trump and his MAGA allies: The slush funds. The tariffs. The apathy. The endless war. The high gas prices. The condescension. The vanity projects. The lack of any thought about what working families are going through on a daily basis.
So today I want to tell you what I am building. Here is what the MI Hope Agenda actually means - in seven pillars, written for the people I love.
🛠️ **Equitable Federal Investment.** Federal dollars should follow the need - not the political map. I have spent years fighting for Michigan to get its fair share of federal investment, and the next chapter of that fight is making sure the dollars reach the communities that have been waiting the longest. Equitable means the ones who have been told to wait don't have to wait anymore.
📈 **Economic Empowerment and Access.** Workforce training is the single fastest way to move someone from struggling to make rent to building a life. Industrial policy is how we make sure the jobs of the next 20 years are jobs in Michigan, not jobs we watch go overseas. I am running to expand access to capital and training in the places that need it most - and to put working people, not billionaires, at the center of economic policy.
🏘️ **Safer Communities.** I've met parents who are anxious every day from the threat of gun violence - that's the reality for so many folks. But it doesn't have to be. Safer communities mean commonsense gun safety laws, fair and accountable policing, and real investment in community-based violence prevention. The conversation about safety has been hijacked by extremists who would rather we accept gun violence than challenge it. We can do better - and we should.
💊 **Health and Family Stability.** Last year, I spoke with a veteran in Michigan - a man who is paralyzed and relies on the federal benefits system he earned by serving this country. He told me he was afraid that the chaotic, right-wing cuts coming out of this administration were going to come for his benefits next. He's been on my mind ever since, because no veteran, no Michigander for that matter, should be afraid that the benefits they earned are going to be ripped away. That's why I'm committed to lowering health care costs and defending Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security.
📚 **Education, Innovation, and STEM Workforce Future.** Michigan is the state that put the world on wheels. The next chapter of that story is going to be forged in areas like aerospace, semiconductors, and advanced manufacturing. I am running to invest in the education and training pipeline that makes sure public schools are funded like the future depends on them, because it does. Since my very first term, I've been fighting for a STEM pipeline that reaches every kid in every Michigan ZIP code, and I want to take that fight to the Senate.
🚰 **Water and Infrastructure.** Clean drinking water is a right. Lead pipes have to go - every single one of them. PFAS contamination has to be confronted, and the communities that have shouldered the worst of environmental injustice deserve more than another study. They deserve action, federal dollars, and real accountability for polluters. Michigan is the Great Lakes state. We should be leading on clean water.
🏡 **Lowering Housing Costs.** I cannot count how many conversations I have had with young Michiganders who feel like buying a home is out of the question. Rent is climbing faster than wages. Seniors on fixed incomes are being priced out of the neighborhoods they raised their kids in. The MI Hope Agenda commits to increasing housing supply, supporting families and seniors and people with disabilities, and rebuilding the pathway to homeownership that used to be a basic part of the American middle class.
This is a big agenda. And it's supposed to be. The challenges Michigan families are facing are not small, and they should not be met with small ideas. Anyone telling you that everything is great right now is either a wealthy crony of Donald Trump or lying.
That's why I keep thinking about the conversations I have been having with Michiganders for years now, especially in the communities that have been asked to wait the longest. This is for you.
Because this campaign isn't about me. It's about us.
It's about every single Michigander who's been left behind, pushed aside, or counted out. Every small-business owner who is trying to keep the lights on. Every parent who wants a better life for their child. Every community that's been ignored or underfunded.
The MI Hope Agenda is for you.
Yes, we've got work to do. And this is Michigan, so I'm going to roll up my sleeves and get it done.
More soon.
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

| Peter--

Pam Bondi was just interviewed by the House Oversight Committee today over her cover up of the Epstein Files.

**Here's what we know:** She is a liar. She deflected. She sat in front of Congress and acted like she bears no responsibility for one of the most disturbing and consequential cover-ups in recent memory — a case involving the sexual abuse and exploitation of young girls, and a network of powerful people who have never faced justice.

Pam Bondi is responsible for that. Her inaction has meant continued silence for survivors, and continued protection for the pedophiles and elites who committed these crimes.

➜ Vote-by-mail is a safe and secure way to vote.
➜ 1 in 3 Americans utilize mail-in voting.
➜ A majority of Americans support vote-by-mail.

I know you’re getting ready for the weekend,
and before I say anything else, I need to ask:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6003?t=1001&akid=1667%2E181023%2E_56Ljh ]Will you make your first contribution today of

When I see a problem, I don’t believe in sitting on the sidelines. I
believe in stepping up and getting to work.

That’s what I’ve done throughout my career — from starting my career in
Alabama to help finish the unfinished business of the civil rights
movement, to protecting the votes and voices of Michiganders and defending
Michigan’s elections as Secretary of State.

And it’s exactly why I’m running for governor now.

But we have to be clear-eyed about the fight ahead. After Donald Trump won
Michigan in 2024, national Republicans targeted our state as one of their
absolute biggest pickup opportunities in the country.

One of the leading Republican candidates has already received $5 million
in support from the DeVos family and built his political career around
spreading lies about the 2020 election. We know more outside money and
more attacks are coming.

That’s why your support matters so much right now.

I’m traveling across Michigan every week talking directly with voters
about what they want for the future of this state, and one thing is clear:
They want steady leadership that will focus on making their lives better.

That’s what I’m fighting for. But campaigns like this aren’t built alone —
they’re built together.

Friend,
I am ready to be the steady, experienced leader New Mexico deserves on day one. I’ve spent my life fighting for working families, and I know firsthand the challenges New Mexicans face every day. With just 4 days left until the primary election, the only way we’ll be able to deliver that kind of leadership is with strong grassroots support from people like you. [**_Will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to help me become the next Governor of New Mexico and move us toward a future where everyone can thrive?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8175?refcode=jtk757-fr-nd&t=2&akid=9936%2E400544%2Ex3xwB3)

As Governor of New Mexico, I will:
* **Ensure** every child in New Mexico — no matter their background — has a fair shot to dream big and reach their full potential through stronger schools, early literacy with dedicated reading coaches, and giving kids the support they need to succeed.

* **Support** New Mexico families by creating jobs, raising wages, lowering costs, and making our state more affordable for working people.

* **Fight** to protect and expand access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico by addressing provider shortages and investing in mental healthcare, substance use treatment, rehabilitation, and housing stability.

* **Focus** every day on stopping violent crime, and addressing the root causes of crime so our communities are safer.

This raises questions about clean-money branding, Wall Street donors, campaign hypocrisy and whether Jackson is borrowing Graham Platner's outsider playbook.

Friend,
Just wanted to make sure you saw my email from earlier.
We have just 48 hours left to meet our end-of-month goal, and we’re still $2,750 short with 60 more grassroots donors needed before the deadline.
If you can contribute $10 or any amount you can, it would mean a lot right now and help us keep building momentum across the district. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak?&amount=10]
We can keep building a campaign rooted in service, accountability, and the belief that this district deserves leadership that actually shows up.

http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak]
Hi friend. Before May ends, I wanted to reflect on what this month has meant for our campaign.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve traveled across Colorado’s 3rd District meeting with farmers, veterans, small business owners, and working families who feel like Washington isn’t listening. I’ve heard concerns about healthcare cuts, rising costs, and rural communities being left behind.
But I’ve also heard something hopeful: people haven’t given up on this district or on each other.
This month reminded me why I’m running — to fight for the people of the Western Slope, not party leadership or corporate interests.
Jeff Hurd continues to support policies that hurt working families. I’m offering a different kind of leadership: grassroots, accountable, and focused on the people who live here.
Before midnight on May 30, we need to raise another $3,500 and bring in 85 more grassroots donors to stay on track. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak?&]
That support will help us keep organizing across all 27 counties to build a campaign strong enough to flip this seat.
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to step in, this is it. Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can before tomorrow night’s deadline? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak?&]

subject: Trump Chose Transparency Over a Payout. His Critics Hate That.
body:
Judicial Watch Sues CIA for Brennan Notes

[INSIDE JW]

TRUMP CHOSE TRANSPARENCY OVER A PAYOUT. HIS CRITICS HATE THAT.

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37953&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1xdXQyaXlzc1dJUSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=bbb82a2dacc6f3dea11e7c26d3fa09a348fef01bc8be52f44f4f86de78d231de]

President Trump rejected potentially billions in damages in his IRS
leak lawsuit for a settlement that would fund justice for alleged
victims of government abuse. Critics now attack the remedy rather than
confront the misconduct it exposes.

I explore this in my column in _The Hill_ this week:

> Last week, the Justice Department announced
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37954&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVzdGljZS5nb3Yvb3BhL3ByL2p1c3RpY2UtZGVwYXJ0bWVudC1hbm5vdW5jZXMtYW50aS13ZWFwb25pemF0aW9uLWZ1bmQ/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=d3d5adee93a931cf1af46fc3eee0b398ab0919662c5cfaf50f6f100f85a82043]
> a new $1.776 billion “anti-weaponization fund” as part of the
> settlement of President Trump’s lawsuit over the illegal leak of
> his tax returns. Trump did something rare in Washington: he walked
> away from potentially billions of dollars of direct damages for
> himself and his company so the federal government would instead set
> up a process to compensate Americans who say they were abused by
> that same government.
>
> That is the truth behind this fund, and it is why so many of
> Trump’s political opponents and critics are now lining up against
> it—they are not objecting because the fund is corrupt, but because
> it exposes misconduct inside the government that was long downplayed
> or ignored.
>
> For years, Americans watched federal agencies turn their power
> against citizens on the wrong side of the prevailing political
> consensus.
>
> Conservatives were targeted by the IRS. Parents were treated as
> threats for speaking out at school board meetings. Prolife advocates
> were dragged into court. Catholics were monitored. Political
> opponents of the Biden administration were treated not simply as
> rivals, but as potential dangers.
>
> President Trump has made clear that this pattern has to end, and the
> White House’s own
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37955&F=T&&hash=61c02c3f8a2acc58983adcb687a75d41fa25c4504da9ee7b5530ee48484a2c27
> sheet
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37956&F=T&&hash=dbb82e5d4d880aa061b8565f7f34564e80da48ba07a63f5ba287ea5fe243cd0b]
> on ending the weaponization of the federal government says his FY
> 2027 budget is meant to restore a government “by and for the
> people,” not one that targets and intimidates them.
>
> Now the anti-weaponization fund is in place, and many of the same
> voices that dismissed earlier complaints about abuse are suddenly
> gravely concerned about the process. Under the Justice
> Department’s settlement announcement, Trump, Donald Trump Jr.,
> Eric Trump and the Trump Organization receive a formal apology for
> the improper handling of his tax information—but no money.
>
> Instead, the government is establishing a structured process to hear
> claims from others who say they suffered political, personal or
> ideological retaliation, and to provide monetary relief or formal
> apologies where warranted. Claims can be filed by anyone who can
> show they were unfairly targeted on political, personal or
> ideological grounds, and the commission must finish its work by late
> 2028 under the settlement.
>
> The fund will draw $1.776 billion from the existing “Judgment
> Fund,” which is used to cover legal settlements against the
> federal government. Participation in the new fund is voluntary,
> there are no partisan requirements for filing a claim, quarterly
> reports are built in, and any money left over ultimately returns to
> the federal government.
>
> I hope those appointed to oversee the compensation fund have a broad
> understanding of the abuses of power and abuse that targeted not
> only Trump and his allies but countless other Americans who would
> have no effective redress of grievances but for this new fund. The
> sooner the leadership and rules are established the better so
> justice can finally flow to the regular people harmed by lawfare.
>
> Judicial Watch represented Ashli Babbitt’s family in the wrongful
> death lawsuit over her outrageous shooting death at the January 6
> protests. Ashli's family had to go through years of administrative
> delays and federal litigation before President Trump's team settled
> the claims for her wrongful death. Other victims of government abuse
> and misconduct should have an easier time getting justice under the
> new compensation fund.
>
> The new compensation fund has significantly more transparency than
> the federal tort claims process the Justice Department already uses
> for considering, settling, or ignoring citizen claims of abuse and
> misconduct by the federal government.
>
> The deeper objection by the DC political-media Borg caterwauling
> about the anti-weaponization fund is not really about dollars and
> cents or transparency. It is about what the fund implicitly
> concedes: that government weaponization is a real problem, and that
> people who were harmed by it deserve an avenue for redress.
> Admitting that premise would mean acknowledging that Trump and his
> allies were abused through the worst government corruption in
> American history, and that citizens on the wrong side of those
> decisions paid a price. For many of Trump’s critics, it is easier
> to attack the remedy than to confront that reality.
>
> Americans across the political spectrum should be able to agree on a
> basic principle: a government that can abuse citizens must also be
> answerable to them. The anti-weaponization fund is one piece of that
> effort.
>
> It signals that if the government targeted you for political
> reasons, you should not be told simply to move on and trust the same
> institutions that failed you. You should be heard. You should have a
> claim. And you should get some modicum of justice under law.
> President Trump and his family gave up countless amounts of money to
> ensure citizen victims of government abuse at least have a chance
> for compensation. He should be praised, not attacked, for this
> selflessness.

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES CIA FOR BRENNAN’S NOTES ON OBAMA-ERA BRIEFINGS

Hillary Clinton cooked up a plan to tie candidate Donald Trump to
Russia, and this plan was discussed in the Oval Office of President
Obama. We’re digging into it.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37948&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtY2lhLWJyZW5uYW4tY29tcGxhaW50LTAxNjMwLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=e16862555a8684109951f1f70e01f018daf3b628fbd02fcaa619985f78f099b6]
against the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) for former CIA Director
John Brennan’s unredacted handwritten notes and related records from
White House briefings in 2016 that referenced intelligence regarding a
Hillary Clinton campaign plan to link then-candidate Donald Trump to

After 30 years, serious questions remain about the federal
government’s handling of the TWA Flight 800 investigation. We are
suing for transparency about how the CIA became involved and how it
reached conclusions that differ so significantly from the accounts of
other experts and more than 200 eyewitnesses.

On July 17, 1996, at 8:31 p.m., TWA Flight 800
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83159&L=37930&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYy1zcGFuLm9yZy9wcm9ncmFtL3B1YmxpYy1hZmZhaXJzLWV2ZW50L3R3YS1mbGlnaHQtODAwLWNyYXNoLzEyMjAwMD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=e0bf64ca2147a3eec9d95e9b98c32aaa2eee21ead19ac18043cdf4e56b3d98ea],
a Boeing 747-131 bound for Paris, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean
minutes after taking off from John F. Kennedy International Airport in
New York City. All 230 people died in the crash, including 212
passengers and 18 crew members.

We filed the lawsuit after the CIA failed to respond to a March 25,
2026, FOIA request for records related to the agency’s decision to
participate in the TWA Flight 800 investigation. The request seeks
records about the CIA’s production of its “witness perception”
animation, including communications with the Federal Bureau of
Investigation (FBI), U.S. Department of Justice, National
Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), White House, National Security
Council, and U.S. Department of Defense.

We are also seeking records regarding the methodology, assumptions,
software, drafts, peer reviews, and public release of the animation,
as well as records concerning the CIA’s analysis of eyewitness
testimony describing ascending streaks of light near the aircraft. In
addition, the request asks for records regarding interagency
coordination, including communications about missile theories,

clean_body: Judicial Watch Sues CIA for Brennan Notes [INSIDE JW] TRUMP CHOSE TRANSPARENCY OVER A PAYOUT. HIS CRITICS HATE THAT. [] President Trump rejected potentially billions in damages in his IRS leak lawsuit for a settlement that would fund justice for alleged victims of government abuse. Critics now attack the remedy rather than confront the misconduct it exposes. I explore this in my column in The Hill this week: Last week, the Justice Department announced [] a new $1.776 billion “anti-weaponization fund” as part of the settlement of President Trump’s lawsuit over the illegal leak of his tax returns. Trump did something rare in Washington: he walked away from potentially billions of dollars of direct damages for himself and his company so the federal government would instead set up a process to compensate Americans who say they were abused by that same government. That is the truth behind this fund, and it is why so many of Trump’s political opponents and critics are now lining up against it—they are not objecting because the fund is corrupt, but because it exposes misconduct inside the government that was long downplayed or ignored. For years, Americans watched federal agencies turn their power against citizens on the wrong side of the prevailing political consensus. Conservatives were targeted by the IRS. Parents were treated as threats for speaking out at school board meetings. Prolife advocates were dragged into court. Catholics were monitored. Political opponents of the Biden administration were treated not simply as rivals, but as potential dangers. President Trump has made clear that this pattern has to end, and the White House’s own [ sheet [] on ending the weaponization of the federal government says his FY 2027 budget is meant to restore a government “by and for the people,” not one that targets and intimidates them. Now the anti-weaponization fund is in place, and many of the same voices that dismissed earlier complaints about abuse are suddenly gravely concerned about the process. Under the Justice Department’s settlement announcement, Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump and the Trump Organization receive a formal apology for the improper handling of his tax information—but no money. Instead, the government is establishing a structured process to hear claims from others who say they suffered political, personal or ideological retaliation, and to provide monetary relief or formal apologies where warranted. Claims can be filed by anyone who can show they were unfairly targeted on political, personal or ideological grounds, and the commission must finish its work by late 2028 under the settlement. The fund will draw $1.776 billion from the existing “Judgment Fund,” which is used to cover legal settlements against the federal government. Participation in the new fund is voluntary, there are no partisan requirements for filing a claim, quarterly reports are built in, and any money left over ultimately returns to the federal government. I hope those appointed to oversee the compensation fund have a broad understanding of the abuses of power and abuse that targeted not only Trump and his allies but countless other Americans who would have no effective redress of grievances but for this new fund. The sooner the leadership and rules are established the better so justice can finally flow to the regular people harmed by lawfare. Judicial Watch represented Ashli Babbitt’s family in the wrongful death lawsuit over her outrageous shooting death at the January 6 protests. Ashli's family had to go through years of administrative delays and federal litigation before President Trump's team settled the claims for her wrongful death. Other victims of government abuse and misconduct should have an easier time getting justice under the new compensation fund. The new compensation fund has significantly more transparency than the federal tort claims process the Justice Department already uses for considering, settling, or ignoring citizen claims of abuse and misconduct by the federal government. The deeper objection by the DC political-media Borg caterwauling about the anti-weaponization fund is not really about dollars and cents or transparency. It is about what the fund implicitly concedes: that government weaponization is a real problem, and that people who were harmed by it deserve an avenue for redress. Admitting that premise would mean acknowledging that Trump and his allies were abused through the worst government corruption in American history, and that citizens on the wrong side of those decisions paid a price. For many of Trump’s critics, it is easier to attack the remedy than to confront that reality. Americans across the political spectrum should be able to agree on a basic principle: a government that can abuse citizens must also be answerable to them. The anti-weaponization fund is one piece of that effort. It signals that if the government targeted you for political reasons, you should not be told simply to move on and trust the same institutions that failed you. You should be heard. You should have a claim. And you should get some modicum of justice under law. President Trump and his family gave up countless amounts of money to ensure citizen victims of government abuse at least have a chance for compensation. He should be praised, not attacked, for this selflessness. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES CIA FOR BRENNAN’S NOTES ON OBAMA-ERA BRIEFINGS Hillary Clinton cooked up a plan to tie candidate Donald Trump to Russia, and this plan was discussed in the Oval Office of President Obama. We’re digging into it. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) for former CIA Director John Brennan’s unredacted handwritten notes and related records from White House briefings in 2016 that referenced intelligence regarding a Hillary Clinton campaign plan to link then-candidate Donald Trump to Russia (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Central Intelligence Agenc [ [ (1:26-cv-01630)). body:
Final Email from the campaign

| |
---
| | Dear Friends, It has certainly been a wild ride since I launched my campaign for Congress in August 2025. Thank you for being a part of the adventure. This will be the last email from my campaign as we shut down operations and turn to supporting Beth Macy’s campaign to replace Ben Cline in Congress. **What we have already done.**
* We changed the Facebook page from “Pete Barlow for Congress” to “From the Valley and For the Valley.” The page will serve as a gathering place for all of us to share information, events, and ideas about supporting an inclusive, people-driven democracy in western Virginia. It is being managed by a team of volunteers who worked on my campaign. You can reach that team via the messenger app. We hope you will stay engaged!
* I am working on Beth Macy’s campaign, helping her connect with voters and community leaders across the district. _Please find an opportunity to meet with Beth._
* My campaign manager, Jayne Docherty, is creating a Substack space called West of the Blue Ridge. My earlier writings and new writings will be hosted there. Jayne will also have a Substack on the site, and we will share news articles and other Substack posts. The goal is to create ground-up political engagement by hosting and sharing news and longer-form opinion pieces specific to western Virginia. _If you write a Substack and want to have it featured on West of the Blue Ridge, please email Jayne at_[ _jayne.docherty@gmail.com_](mailto:jayne.docherty@gmail.com) _._

**What you can expect next from the campaign.**
* _We will shut down the campaign on June 15, 2026._ No donations will be processed after that date. We ran a frugal campaign, and thanks to your support, we will be able to close the campaign without debt. _Big thanks to all who set up automatic donations. You helped us make our closeout plans with confidence._ If you want to cancel your automatic contributions immediately, please visit ActBulue and follow the instructions. If you need help, contact Jayne at [jayne.docherty@gmail.com](mailto:jayne.dochertu@gmail.com).
* We will shut down the campaign website [pete-barlow.com](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/gMH8n2gG2s4twgjMs4EquA~~/AAUS1hA~/oKhun1PBSoukrtx-OzTZo6cHTxq5AjQQGkz2QsITSTjdTzjgm79eIFo8FUo9J-Uktg4PQ31DctcPJyw1J2V0BRF13wkpfvkbWw0xNySgGHM~) by the end of June.

**What about the future?** I have not ruled out running for office in the future, but if I do, I will know a lot more about what to expect. We are saving all of our data, and you will be the first to know if I do run again. Meanwhile, let’s each dare to be in the arena defending democracy, building community, and promoting laws and policies that work for all. With Gratitude,

Peter, I went back and forth on if I should send you this or not. Not because I didn't know what to say, but because I knew how much it would hurt to say it. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. But I'm trusting these words will reach you the way they need to.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/N4Im1qtq_OlbDf_4Pj0JWuChPmIybkFXobrV8mp_WO2JzY_l2PW5Ng4_SwOos0epzt7ylH49_UkQZZiwoTL8IxQNHo3BP4qBEFb6C0Y1dyXf99-eo32FFeqMV8FbOipVNm-72vdXGoFqPNPVlCwhno6R9ITGrbds-geh89i0_z121cuZ-YHSbgEOvh1pzL-Nb6Zyr5aIo-FAwWOzRXPGSWZdav9D96kliwjyGUqWQPij3_xDNPyyGeBw6poKcHezf_rG6kjv_xRYUf26tj-REXEhKt-QsfdpZkfs8TPz46np8k5ssRUU5cnmFsoEGXaX54BCBgX156fG3zIOyjEHxlxjZ4hFKz4EcPTc7j7kDykZsxsFF7z8LOvbG7UfUgyMXGKj97ZBaKDwJKqldzA-IOHCVpHWooVqpwAOfkD6Ayf96rxlvVZZzheZAlGA4mSgUURG9uvMT1Bwq8y45JIEMv3xzpQiwa2V2tr8dyfdr7keHp1W_cKcCgJf-lYkW4p5S-1PLwavSVMVJf4R0Na7O7HT38vowq3ftatZEugELfXoRGeX-EbXo3d-qH5fcM3llMAj9AcZ3O9ABTXR6kmWcyh-s7Mq9S_fIuQSTipWSovwIbtuZQk0wNoBWXfAzdeRISMODoiVoStyoEGkfU0RsVrF_Pq7Zolrli038xPVDh0h6Xm-NPjowgdQWsJDDYus0ATO5sReH1DSzOqkuLoKECesJNg5EcfgYGwS7Sakk_BRRl-ci9ImMrLmJwnqVHCtIvt1AEfev1v3WRUqdhd8hx472Va-5VW6yS2nKvVO_jgEZcs/JUipKK_U4a1pQiOfK_QPWNLuZNTAPLMK/21) It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/6TGofDqxWW0oDjlI0Z1-eADf5Vo5hPTGWiSf9OE_es33otEjAVl52CHE3UcUlmzPzj6b9TfKdityUB7jE6hOYqMC1Hg84iNVtBILVNn5SmmnpitqeNbQO29K5NmEV_gJVpIra5lnj1h3r0bVrlmnoGMPpCWkAgMFnj714spSjA7QN3v5WsOqGde-2B184bULJ3-vcrnLkAVz_WMsxZoZ4-NXGqYciaew7Ke9hESKwuHSvl5W1LbNRa-3uhRlf6Zyqyo2WGticCeHkkhPQSMHvb82BETeJRh8gM3EVLDRvxS1KO-nu-YsuKBw3fQ_qJWoxTFh-O6Ju4S_8nyxrjZFiBqkPNcGBc09UOi4whhaLktiVAPJzrq2V5TPHqUGY7g2DeU9-x1O9sPM5VmzH04GjZpxO3rZZNFM5-_cPLF1NzRswDOL1m5a9mAcmkwoys_fH7ItE39VVpIOh_QJcjqdIRViX8NkT5FgRUJDPcYo-lbwHVTyiXeZXaDjTpR2Oy3M3YEpp-wJVYxDOgDgj1hYRCY7RXHlCgBytFj5tPsEKLclQ2rG2ggMPN4q0Kok2p8C9s6VdKMZbdbGdvFf1C0u1dyy8R8ZGJM3vfZn51PSHx7uGfWrYWwPhJ8A6YdejJbKUNT2A-tLuOlLiwtxqbb8Yv317f4zNWjknk2GVY_C6r3W4y6JJQjBQaLocWfRrtIT058FtaQMIS8DawKlqphC5-5MXNQ_CcwQHIZ_oho9jbmcmHq_ClYpIMenw6JVq-QYgypu0kQeYAYx5frk35e1nuIgnovWaOmonNuEikebzLXAqco/d7ZY88bBez19ykhOAP5HLOhJs-evUvRC/21) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. A war in the Middle East, an economy on a knife's edge, and a president who keeps making headlines he didn't mean to make, and somehow the sharpest commentary this week didn't come from a cable panel or a newspaper column. It came from a zoo in Bangladesh, a nature documentary that should not exist, and a song you already know every word to without knowing why. David Shuster has counted down the five funniest AI satire clips of the week, and we are not going to spoil a single one of them for you. We'll just say this: one of them involves an albino buffalo, one of them is narrated like you're watching prestige wildlife television, and one of them turns a very ordinary day of the week into the most damning two minutes you'll see all month.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Fr05wJ-yaLODj16iELuCU-CEBNtIUwDNW6i-9Bc7H4c?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199798115)
It only escalates from there. The number two clip drags a certain administration into a fashion-world showdown with a magazine whose name you will not forget, and the number one entry, all the way from Canada, imagines what happens when the people demanding the release of certain files finally meet someone with the technology to get answers the hard way.
There's a chorus. You will sing it. You will be a little ashamed of how fast you learned it.
Watch the full countdown to see which clip Shuster crowned number one, why it's the one everyone's going to be quoting by Monday, and what a bucket of fried chicken has to do with any of it.

_**Cliff 's Note**_: Look, here's the thing about authoritarians: they can survive a lot of things, but they cannot survive being laughed at.
Mockery is the one weapon that gets under the skin, because it tells the strongman the one thing he can't stand to hear, which is that he's ridiculous. That's what makes David Shuster's Weekender so much more than a highlight reel. Week after week, David and the artists he's spotlighting are doing the work the legacy press won't: refusing to sanewash this, refusing to pretend any of it is normal, and turning Trump, Lindsey Graham, Stephen Miller, and the whole crew into exactly what they are, which is punchlines.
That's not a distraction from the fight. That's the fight.

According to a new Pine Tree State Poll, a States of Opinion Project conducted by the University of New Hampshire Survey Center, Graham Platner has a 73 percent favorability rating among likely voters in Maine's Democratic primary.
Incumbent Sen. Susan Collins (R), on the other hand, has a 65 percent favorability rating among those who are likely to vote in Maine's Republican primary election.
In a head-to-head match up, Platner holds a several point lead over Sen. Collins, albeit by a slightly smaller margin than several months ago, as more undecided voters have moved to support the sitting senator, as well as some of those who were previously interested in supporting another candidate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8f0f0855-ff12-4425-961f-f17108bb1602?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Source:**[University of New Hampshire Survey Center, Pine Tree State Poll, a States of Opinion Project](https://substack.com/redirect/feb724bf-8fcf-4dc7-9cf9-8d76fe5baeed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For Maine's gubernatorial race, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson and former Director of the Maine Centers for Disease Control Nirav Shah are neck-and-neck in the Democratic primary, as former Assistant U.S. Secretary of State Robert Charles holds a strong lead on the Republican side.
Earlier this year, Shah was shown to hold a sizable lead over Jackson, but they are now tied as several percentage points worth of support have shifted away from Secretary of State Shenna Bellows.
Both former Speaker of the Maine House of Representatives Hannah Pingree and energy executive Angus King III also appear to have gained some support but to a much less notable degree.
Many of these changes can likely be attributed to the fact that the share of undecided voters is now less than half of what it was earlier this year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9bf41246-74bf-4383-8e98-3de11e69c37a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Source:**[University of New Hampshire Survey Center, Pine Tree State Poll, a States of Opinion Project](https://substack.com/redirect/feb724bf-8fcf-4dc7-9cf9-8d76fe5baeed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Among Republicans, Charles' lead has remained consistent with support expanding from 28 percent to 37 percent.
That said, healthcare executive Jonathan Bush has gained significant ground over the past several months, going from controlling just 5 percent of the field to 18 percent.
Also gaining ground was businessman Ben Midgley, who nearly doubled his support from 6 percent to 11 percent.
Former Maine Senate Majority Leader Garrett Mason lost ground over the past several months, however, with the share of respondents expressing interest in voting for him in the primary dropping from 12 percent to 9 percent.
Most of these changes are likely due to the massive drop in the share of voters expected to participate in the Republican primary who are unsure of the candidate they want to support, as this figure has plummeted from 31 percent to just 9 percent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/522dd234-bc7c-4b02-8652-1f0871c474fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Source:**[University of New Hampshire Survey Center, Pine Tree State Poll, a States of Opinion Project](https://substack.com/redirect/feb724bf-8fcf-4dc7-9cf9-8d76fe5baeed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This survey has a margin of error of +/- 2.6 percent. 1,397 Mainers completed the survey between May 21 and May 25.
595 likely Democratic primary voters were included in the sample, as well as 465 likely Republican primary voters.
**[Click Here to Read the Full Results of the Poll](https://substack.com/redirect/feb724bf-8fcf-4dc7-9cf9-8d76fe5baeed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Early voting for the June 9, 2026 primary election has already begun.
Requests for an absentee ballot must be received by a voter's municipality by the close of business on Thursday, June 4. In-person absentee voting will be available through this same date.
Maine citizens who are not yet registered to vote may do so until the close of polls on election day.
Anyone who is unsure of their voter registration status may contact their local municipal clerk's office to check.
Contact information for all Maine municipal clerks and registrars is available **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/d9acd31f-0be2-432c-bfff-f359842c787e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. A statewide online lookup tool is not currently available.
The June 9 primary election will make use of ranked choice voting, meaning that voters will have the option to express support on their ballot for multiple candidates.
In the event that one candidate does not receive at least 50 percent of the votes cast, the candidate with the least amount of votes will be knocked out of the running. Votes will then be distributed to whichever candidates were marked as a second choice on ballots cast by those supporting the eliminated candidate.
This process continues until one candidate emerges with majority support.
When filling out a ranked choice ballot, voters may rank multiple candidates, vote only for a first choice selection, or fill out all ranking slots in favor of one candidate.
