By Libby Palanza, Maine Wire Reporter May 29 | | | | | | | | | | | According to a new Pine Tree State Poll, a States of Opinion Project conducted by the University of New Hampshire Survey Center, Graham Platner has a 73 percent favorability rating among likely voters in Maine's Democratic primary. Incumbent Sen. Susan Collins (R), on the other hand, has a 65 percent favorability rating among those who are likely to vote in Maine's Republican primary election. In a head-to-head match up, Platner holds a several point lead over Sen. Collins, albeit by a slightly smaller margin than several months ago, as more undecided voters have moved to support the sitting senator, as well as some of those who were previously interested in supporting another candidate. | | ---|---|--- Source: For Maine's gubernatorial race, former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson and former Director of the Maine Centers for Disease Control Nirav Shah are neck-and-neck in the Democratic primary, as former Assistant U.S. Secretary of State Robert Charles holds a strong lead on the Republican side. Earlier this year, Shah was shown to hold a sizable lead over Jackson, but they are now tied as several percentage points worth of support have shifted away from Secretary of State Shenna Bellows. Both former Speaker of the Maine House of Representatives Hannah Pingree and energy executive Angus King III also appear to have gained some support but to a much less notable degree. Many of these changes can likely be attributed to the fact that the share of undecided voters is now less than half of what it was earlier this year. | | ---|---|--- Source: Among Republicans, Charles' lead has remained consistent with support expanding from 28 percent to 37 percent. That said, healthcare executive Jonathan Bush has gained significant ground over the past several months, going from controlling just 5 percent of the field to 18 percent. Also gaining ground was businessman Ben Midgley, who nearly doubled his support from 6 percent to 11 percent. Former Maine Senate Majority Leader Garrett Mason lost ground over the past several months, however, with the share of respondents expressing interest in voting for him in the primary dropping from 12 percent to 9 percent. Most of these changes are likely due to the massive drop in the share of voters expected to participate in the Republican primary who are unsure of the candidate they want to support, as this figure has plummeted from 31 percent to just 9 percent. | | ---|---|--- Source: This survey has a margin of error of +/- 2.6 percent. 1,397 Mainers completed the survey between May 21 and May 25. 595 likely Democratic primary voters were included in the sample, as well as 465 likely Republican primary voters. Early voting for the June 9, 2026 primary election has already begun. Requests for an absentee ballot must be received by a voter's municipality by the close of business on Thursday, June 4. In-person absentee voting will be available through this same date. Maine citizens who are not yet registered to vote may do so until the close of polls on election day. Anyone who is unsure of their voter registration status may contact their local municipal clerk's office to check. Contact information for all Maine municipal clerks and registrars is available . A statewide online lookup tool is not currently available. The June 9 primary election will make use of ranked choice voting, meaning that voters will have the option to express support on their ballot for multiple candidates. In the event that one candidate does not receive at least 50 percent of the votes cast, the candidate with the least amount of votes will be knocked out of the running. Votes will then be distributed to whichever candidates were marked as a second choice on ballots cast by those supporting the eliminated candidate. This process continues until one candidate emerges with majority support. When filling out a ranked choice ballot, voters may rank multiple candidates, vote only for a first choice selection, or fill out all ranking slots in favor of one candidate. Hey folks,
I sat down with **Paulina Mangubat** , Deputy Chief Mobilization Officer at the DNC, after she found herself at the center of one of the internet's weirdest political pile-ons. What started as a conversation about a viral Democrats account post turned into something much bigger: how Democrats communicate, why authenticity matters, and what it actually takes to break through in today's media environment. We talked about online attacks, political messaging, wedding announcements, and why being human online is still one of the most powerful things you can do.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:06**] Paulina joins the show, and we dive straight into the viral Democrats account post that triggered a response from some of the most powerful figures in MAGA world.
* [**00:05:15**] The conversation turns personal as Paulina responds to attacks about her appearance, relationship status, and the bizarre internet backlash that followed.
* [**00:09:00**] We discuss why Democrats have to stop sounding like institutions and start communicating like real people if they want to connect with voters again.
* [**00:16:00**] Paulina pulls back the curtain on how the DNC revamped its content operation after 2024, speeding up approvals and embracing a more aggressive digital strategy.
* [**00:22:30**] We close with a bigger conversation about the future of Democratic organizing, digital-first leadership, and why online engagement matters more than ever.

This episode is about more than one viral tweet. It's about what happens when politics collides with culture, when institutions learn to move at internet speed, and when people refuse to let bad-faith attacks define them. If you care about Democratic messaging, digital organizing, or simply want an honest conversation about navigating today's political landscape, this is one you won't want to miss. We know your inbox is probably full of messages just like this, but let us explain why this one is different.
As one of the ONLY first-term Democratic Senators up for reelection, MAGA thinks I’m the one to beat. President Trump has signaled that Colorado is one of his top targets. And Lauren Boebert’s hand-picked candidate, Mark Baisley, is determined to rubber-stamp Trump’s ruthless agenda.

Friends, Join us tomorrow (5/30) at 3:30PM in Biddeford for a cup of coffee and conversation at _Time and Tide Coffee_ , 35 Maine Street. To RSVP: [**https://www.costelloforsenate.com/.../meet-and-greet-with...**](https://us.list-manage.com/1uSc70cV6rB?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36) Also, below is a link to a more extensive and substantive press (Maine Public Television) interview with David regarding his US Senate campaign to defeat Senator Susan Collins. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=CmaNs-_Wvfo&ra=m](https://us.list-manage.com/10aua4LySdT?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36)
Additionally, below is a text copy of a recent _Bangor Daily News_ Op Ed written and submitted by David.

Thank you,Team Costello **Experience should matter in Maine’s Senate primary** _David Costello of Brunswick is a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate._ While many, including most in the press, have essentially [declared](https://us.list-manage.com/1BBX60_NCJL?e=5d7176e969&c2id=0715660f99493bd2d61bdbd7e3d6dd36) Maine’s Democratic U.S. Senate primary over, there’s still time for voters to consider whether the Democratic Party’s presumptive nominee is the best person to take on Sen. Susan Collins in November. Perceptions of political viability can, and often do, change overnight.I believe that my personal story, education, and government experience contrasts more sharply with that of Sen. Collins than does Graham Platner’s. My lived experience is rooted in many of the same challenges working-class Mainers face every day, and my extensive government service is broader, deeper and more hands-on than Sen. Collins’. Moreover, I believe that my experiences equip me with the kind of knowledge and perspective sorely needed in Washington today.I was born in Bangor and raised in Old Town by my mother and mill-working grandparents. My father, an Army veteran and labor organizer, died at the age of 31 due to hazardous working conditions he faced as a teenager. I know what it’s like to have to hustle to pay bills, compile years of debt and go long periods without health insurance and healthcare.Like many in Maine, I began working at an early age and worked my way through the University of Maine, George Washington University and the London School of Economics. And I subsequently served for more than 30 years in senior-level government and non-governmental organization positions, both in the United States and abroad.These positions included serving as a top aide to Maine’s secretary of state, the mayor of Baltimore and governor of Maryland; as a deputy and acting secretary of the Maryland Department of the Environment; and as a county program manager and regional team leader for the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). These positions involved implementing and managing, not simply legislating or talking about, complex multimillion-dollar programs and operations.These programs and operations included working closely with the U.S. Army, State Department, United Nations and foreign aid organizations overseas — and various state and local government agencies, businesses and non-governmental organizations in Maine, Maryland and elsewhere.They are programs and operations that resulted in election and motor vehicle safety reforms in Maine; improved schools and family assistance programs in Baltimore; the implementation of ambitious job creation, education, healthcare, crime reduction and environmental protection programs in Maryland; and the completion of more than 3,500 peace and community-building projects in conflict-torn Cambodia, Haiti, Bosnia, Croatia, Kosovo and Serbia.I believe experience matters, but so too does my decades-long commitment to substantially reforming our nation’s governing policies, practices, and institutions and eliminating the excessive and corrupting influence that money, wealth and disinformation have over our politics and government. Like many Democrats, I am fully committed to enacting far-reaching legislative and constitutional reforms, among them: Medicare for All; universal childcare; expanded Social Security benefits; a national minimum living wage; increased taxes on the wealthy; a ban on gerrymandering; federal clean elections financing; comprehensive immigration reform; judicial and legislative term limits; codification of Roe v. Wade; an assault weapons ban; and an aggressive national climate action plan.Reforms designed to not only salvage our democracy, but to also better protect our rights and freedoms and to enable us to finally tackle such pressing challenges as: unaffordable housing and healthcare; insufficient retirement security; economic inequality; gun violence; shoddy infrastructure; and climate change. Because only then are we likely to achieve the more perfect union envisioned by our most thoughtful founders and forebears.

36% of voters are still completely undecided — let’s fix that.
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4832%2E898137%2E3aKdgD)
I’m going to be completely straight with you. You know I usually hate the whole asking for money routine — honestly, it’s my absolute _least_ favorite part of this job. But we just looked at the latest numbers from the field, and I need to fill you in on what’s actually happening out here.
Right now, we are statistically tied with our opponent. **A total dead heat**.
On one hand, that’s incredibly exciting because it proves we can absolutely win this thing. But on the other hand, it means every single conversation and every single voter matters right now.
Here is the real kicker: a massive **36% of voters across Michigan are still completely undecided**.
That means more than a third of the state is sitting on the fence, waiting to see who shows up, who listens, and who speaks common sense. We cannot afford to let my Trump-endorsed opponent and his dark-money super PACs be the only ones reaching them. They are already flooding the airwaves with millions of dollars to buy this seat.
I don't take a single dime from corporate PACs, which means I don’t answer to them — I answer to you. But it also means building this campaign brick by brick relies entirely on regular people pitching in when it counts.
To go toe-to-toe and reach those undecided voters in all 83 counties, we need to scale up our operations immediately.

body:
Rent is brutal. Debt is crushing. Young people are being priced out of their future—a future already threatened by climate disasters.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/12MCpiPNn1r?e=8c53948e4c&c2id=06d66eac9b545d55bb613c1fdc65532c)
| | | | | |
# Enough is enough. It’s time we fought back.
---
| | Hello friends,
Rent is brutal. Debt is crushing. Young people are being priced out of their future—a future already threatened by climate disasters. Meanwhile, civilians, mostly women and children, continue to die in wars that leave entire communities traumatized for generations.
Here at home, Donald Trump is trampling on our rights and enriching himself and his allies. Yet too often, the opposition refuses to fight with the urgency this moment demands.
Why?
Because the same corporate and special interests that dominate our political system are funding both parties and wield too much influence on them. The same parties that are funding Trump are also funding a good number of Democrats in Congress. According to [**TrackAIPAC**](https://us.list-manage.com/KyrYJ_E59XF?e=8c53948e4c&c2id=06d66eac9b545d55bb613c1fdc65532c) , both California senators and 8 Republicans and 41 Democrats in Congress all receive money from pro-Israel PACs.
I say enough is enough.
We cannot keep sending the same people to Washington and expect different results.
We need representatives who answer only to voters—not corporate PACs, billionaires, or the powerful Israel lobby.
That's why I'm running for Congress. I don't take corporate PAC or AIPAC money. My campaign is powered by working people who believe that government should work for all of us.
This campaign is built around three simple priorities: **PEOPLE**. **PEACE**. **PLANET**.

I'm fighting for:

| A personal note from Steve | Before June 2nd
---|---
Dear Friend, I wrote this because I do not want this moment to pass quietly. You get a lot of campaign emails. I know that. Most of them are overly urgent and instantly forgettable.
| | ★ |
---|---|---
Deadlines. Buttons. Exclamation points. The usual performance. **This is not that.** I wrote you a real note because **June 2nd is almost here** , and after that, this race moves on with us or without us.
|
---
Please read what I wrote | [Read My Message](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=bd83760c38374855adb301a5070fbcec&_e=5zQNeY7kN4vQQBLw7YZpLK0gnhX6cYVApmOeM_LRB-l21iIs00x0qMAUSTRv2ExjKhuRBflVnJsvxmvBqrDtlvFkGyr175Tn48aBkyJmfjp1pzME-trj4OFAhvM5QHqk_TejYmU_MMEPs2PT2jOPieegWrJrNSeKrYP6H7glDNu8E2IaHkw1Qd2XYsZ6YVxwBU2KxQvbMZ7ZbbCD9F7KkPUlcMgo6SoGS83te7mGSH3wyMcRrLWk_aEbIFGeGk7ZJc0GZMq3TyB4S43l1ym-XEPg-xcLnzu0R5r1l-RqBIqieGv3PsI6kl7PVKs9Z8TdDLIQ9T4xawPa4-0M5hAbuLUMQJKRsutMPsdv7EB2S5-Q5MC3ZwmaMHQ5PoXs_-Ni8lQxEO83yy2bWlkymVCJ7VlrdzroFPfT1BQC23mmV9g5JV0-7nZUYu61k1lUpNE0UntbOMdGzTWx9Li3JVm8DRF8Rzb2f3fjtinnfNTVdsQ%3D)
---

| There is no automatic Republican nominee in California. There is no second chance if we fall short. There is no clever explanation that will make up for failing to do everything possible while there was still time.
---
**That is the brutal, unavoidable fact.** And frankly, I do not want this to be the last serious message I send to Americans across the country about this campaign because Democrats managed to stop us before November. **That would be a bitter, ridiculous ending to a fight we can absolutely win.**
| Before the window closes Help me keep this campaign moving. | [Stand With Me](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=bd83760c38374855adb301a5070fbcec&_e=5zQNeY7kN4vQQBLw7YZpLK0gnhX6cYVApmOeM_LRB-l21iIs00x0qMAUSTRv2ExjKhuRBflVnJsvxmvBqrDtlvFkGyr175Tn48aBkyJmfjp1pzME-trj4OFAhvM5QHqk_TejYmU_MMEPs2PT2jOPieegWrJrNSeKrYP6H7glDNu8E2IaHkw1Qd2XYsZ6YVxwBU2KxQvbMZ7ZbbCD9F7KkPUlcMgo6SoGS83te7mGSH3wyMcRrLWk_aEbIFGeGk7ZJc0GZMq3TyB4S43l1ym-XEPg-xcLnzu0R5r1l-RqBIqieGv3PsI6kl7PVKs9Z8TdDLIQ9T4xawPa4-0M5hAbuMuPzsIDAZMsCopxWLR_4V6_HZYPU1D-xp3pTbphr4e4kLoD5XgnSnRZmXwfNJd0mtq7FhKHzyXWZXdJrCS4aLietTdB3y_DLcZpcHftBgDRb7XPZ8kee_YfkX2UUAynb6wyjXqwHkaZlw_xfwdRrfk%3D)
---
So before you scroll past another campaign email, I want you to read the note I wrote. It explains exactly where this race stands, why Democrats want us buried before June 2nd, and why I believe they are terrified of facing us one-on-one in November. They should be.
|
---
_Thank you,_
_Steve Hilton_
_Authorized by Hilton for Governor 2026_

U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) introduced legislation this week to combat the rapid rise in youth gambling.

The bipartisan legislation by Britt and U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Gaming Advertisement to Minors Enforcement (GAME) Act, would prohibit social media companies and other advertising websites from targeting minors with sports betting through online advertising.

The Federal Trade Commission would be responsible for enforcing the law, which would begin one year after enactment. Failure to comply could result in civil financial penalties and injunctive relief sought in court.

Under the GAME Act, repeat offenders can be referred to the Department of Justice, which may impose financial penalties of up to $100,000 for each advertisement that promotes sports gambling and is shown to a minor. In cases where thousands of advertisements are shown to minors, the financial penalties could become substantial.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt recently secured a total of $426,000 in appropriations funding for the Coosa County Emergency Management Agency (EMA) through two Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations bills.

According to Senator Britt’s office, the funding includes $126,000 through the FY2026 Homeland Security Appropriations Act and an additional $300,000 through the FY2026 Labor, Health and Human Services, and Related Agencies Act.

The funding will support the purchase of a new generator and ambulance-related equipment and procurement for the Coosa County EMA headquarters. County officials have been working to strengthen the emergency management center to better coordinate planning and response efforts during severe weather events and other emergencies.

Coosa County EMA consists of a small paid staff supported by a network of volunteers who assist in emergency response operations throughout the county.

WASHINGTON, D.C. - Sen. Katie Britt from Alabama introduced legislation that would require all U.S. employers to use E-Verify to check if workers are legally allowed to work in the country.

Britt, who serves on the Senate Judiciary Committee, introduced the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026. While some states and federal agencies already require E-Verify, there's no national rule making it mandatory everywhere.

E-Verify is a system that lets employers confirm whether someone is eligible to work in the United States. Britt's bill would make the program permanent, increase penalties for hiring people who aren't authorized to work and add stronger fraud prevention measures. The legislation would also stop states from blocking employers from using E-Verify.

Kennedy by statute,** requiring congressional action to change the name, and found the board vote to close the center improper and ill-formed. The ruling mandates Kennedy Center officials complete all required planning, environmental reviews, secure necessary approvals and permits, and obtain express congressional authorization before proceeding with closure and renovation.

clean_body: The first major test of our campaign is approaching, and we need your help. | Fellow Patriot, The first major test of our campaign is approaching, and we need your help. May 31st is our very first fundraising deadline, and it's make-or-break for our campaign. If you’re able, I’m humbly asking you for a donation of anything you can spare before it’s too late. My opponent is well-funded and well-connected. He has wealthy donors bankrolling his campaign whose interests do not align with the Hudson Valley. Look, I am not beholden to a political party or special interests. My loyalty is to the families in New York’s 18th District. I was born and raised in the Hudson Valley. I know personally the values the community holds dear-integrity, hard work, and accountability. As a 29-year-old, I have seen what many young families I grew up with have had to endure due to rising costs and the cost of living in our state. It pains me to see them leaving our community for more affordable areas. I hope to fix that so that generations of families, like mine, can call the Hudson Valley home. Fellow Patriot, I know many folks do not have extra funds to spare, so I don’t take asking for money lightly. But if you’re able, - I am counting on your support to fuel our campaign before our first major fundraising deadline on 5/31 so that we can bolster our efforts during the summer months before Election Day. Thank you, Jackie Mary All The Way With JMA | | Paid for by Jackie Auringer for Congress Don't want to receive any more of our emails? We hate to see you go: .

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: 192 pages. Not a single mention of Gaza.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
There’s a lot to be said about what’s in it, but what’s most appalling to me is what’s not.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260529-6289-footer&t=1&akid=6289%2E420207%2EelWB3Z)
Peter,
You’ve probably seen the news about the DNC releasing its post-2024 autopsy last week. There’s a lot to be said about what’s in it, but what’s most appalling to me is what’s _not._
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260529-2.C4WPqn&refcode=em20260529-6289&t=2&akid=6289%2E420207%2EelWB3Z)
**In 192 pages, the DNC autopsy doesn’t mention the words ‘Gaza’ to ‘Israel’ anywhere in text.** Not one word. It completely erases the genocide of the Palestinian people that’s still happening to this day — and which undoubtedly played a role in the outcome of the 2024 election.
I’ve been an organizer my entire career, and if there’s one thing I know for sure it’s that you cannot build a winning coalition by leaving communities behind. **And the lack of transparency in this report threatens to take us back to where we were when we lost to Donald Trump two years ago.**
If we’re serious about taking back the House in November — and about building a governing coalition that’s strong enough to enact progressive priorities like Medicare For All, just immigration reform, and more — we have to be serious about this too.
The people who we need to power this movement to victory in November are not going to show up for a party that plays it safe and looks away from injustice. **They’re going to show up for something real and honest that sees them, hears them, and refuses to forget who they’re fighting for.**
That’s the kind of party I’m working to build, and I’m going to keep speaking out when we fall short. But in order to grow our progressive movement, I’m counting on your grassroots support.
[**With our campaign’s end-of-month deadline coming up on Sunday night, can I count on you to pitch in $3 to help us reach our $34,000 goal and keep up the fight?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260529-2.C4WPqn&refcode=em20260529-6289&amount=3&t=3&akid=6289%2E420207%2EelWB3Z)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

True leadership isn't defined by the speeches you give on a cable news channel. It's defined by how you show up for your neighbors when the cameras are turned off.
Throughout my time in Middle Tennessee, I've dedicated myself to working with vital local organizations like Second Harvest Food Bank and the Nashville Rescue Mission. When you look into the eyes of a parent trying to figure out how to feed their kids, or someone experiencing homelessness on our streets, it changes how you view public policy. You realize that the failures of Washington have devastating, real-world human costs.
**Let 's put community back at the center of politics. [Help us spread this message across TN-04 by contributing $10 or more today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1c1152d8-4a6e-477d-b11f-0dd635f07664?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [🚨CLICK HERE🚨](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1c1152d8-4a6e-477d-b11f-0dd635f07664?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e5807af-d37e-4766-928a-17380fc13095?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
While career politicians like Scott DesJarlais spend their time sitting quietly on Capitol Hill, our communities are quietly hurting. We need leaders who understand empathy, who have looked local poverty in the face, and who are determined to legislatively dismantle it.
**I 'M THAT LEADER.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0215412c-98c0-44fb-8d97-c2c01989e40e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[PUT A REAL LEADER IN CONGRESS HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1c1152d8-4a6e-477d-b11f-0dd635f07664?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm running for Congress to take that community-first mentality to Washington. We can build communities where food banks don't have to fill the massive gaps left by a failing government, and families can live dignified lives.
Let's keep that fight alive, right here and now, before DesJarlais can even attempt to serve another year for nothing! They don't show up because unity exposes their intentions.
It's time for a change.

body:
An entire generation of Texans has grown up under Abbott’s failed leadership.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
I graduated from high school in 1992, Peter.
_**That’s how long Greg Abbott has been in power.**_ Think about that for a second.
An entire generation of Texans has grown up under the same failed leadership. The same corruption. The same billionaire-first agenda that has left working families fighting harder for less.
And after all these years, too many Texans have started to believe this is just how things are supposed to be.
But I refuse to accept that. **I’m fighting back.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260529_3_grad.ll15eG&refcode=em20260529-1228&amount=5&t=1&akid=1228%2E299639%2ElxFw4b)
Because I know that we can defeat Greg Abbott. We can lower costs, fund our schools, and put healthcare in reach of working families.
Texans deserve a new governor who fights for working people instead of billionaire donors and corporate interests. **That’s why I’m running to make this Greg Abbott’s last term.**
**[If you’re ready for a new generation of leadership in Texas, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can today?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260529_3_grad.ll15eG&refcode=em20260529-1228&amount=5&t=2&akid=1228%2E299639%2ElxFw4b)**

Thank you,
Gina

We are making strong progress, and I am grateful for the support that has gotten us this far. At the same time, we are still just short of where we need to be to finish out this month with confidence. Moments like this may not seem significant on the surface, but they shape what comes next. Falling short simply makes the path forward more difficult than it needs to be. It also lets Democrats gain momentum. I know, I don 't want that to happen either. | As this month closes out, it's important to show conservatives all over the nation that we are working hard to save this country. And I believe in people stepping in when they can, especially at moments like this. If you have been thinking about getting involved, this is the time to do it. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: I was treated horribly by my own Party.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
I just was.
#
I was treated horribly by my own Party. I just was.
I was told that I was an enemy of my Party.
That I was going to be the reason why the Right won.
That the entire future of the country was in balance and that _I_ was the reason why we would lose.
What was hurtful was that they were telling me this because of what I believed.
I was being told this because of my commitment to trans rights, Medicare for All — which is seen as radical communist propaganda — and workers' rights.
In the Democratic Party we have a broad coalition, and so some of the most conservative members of the Party.... it can be hard.
But **the brutal reality is that we are all that we have**. We will not survive apart.
I know. I’ve been there. It feels very difficult and challenging when the people who are diminishing you are the ones that you need.
We have to learn how to hold conflict, and hold together in conflict.
Our main project now is to **unite the working class in this country against a fascist agenda**. Period.

Friend, This month alone, we saw new voter suppression laws, attacks on fair maps, new barriers targeting young and minority voters, and more state-level efforts designed to quietly weaken democratic participation. Most of it got buried under the avalanche of bad news hitting Americans every single day. body:
#
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20260529-707&t=1&akid=707%2E34582%2EYYJ1ia)
Peter,
It’s Beto.
Something powerful is happening in Texas right now.
[**Before I tell you more about the shift I see happening in Texas, will you donate $5 split between Small Town PAC and Gina’s campaign for governor?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20260529-707&t=2&akid=707%2E34582%2EYYJ1ia)
For years, we’ve been doing the hard work to flip Texas — a state where Republicans have always tried to make voting harder. **We’ve registered voters, recruited candidates for every place on the ballot, and found ways to overcome the extreme voter suppression from the Republicans in power. And now, this race has the potential to capitalize on all of the hard work, all of the campaigns that have come before, to break through and win.**
Back in March, Gina won her Democratic primary, which sparked real energy across the state. From Amarillo to Brownsville, El Paso to Austin, she and other Democrats on the ballot helped generate turnout numbers we haven’t seen in decades.
This shift is showing up beyond this race, too. **Over the last few weeks, Texans have been voting for change in local elections across the state.**
It’s not a guarantee of what happens in November, but it’s a sign we can’t ignore. Texans are paying attention, they’re engaged, and they’re ready for real leadership.
Because after more than a decade of Greg Abbott, Texans are looking around and asking a simple question. _What are we getting from Abbott’s leadership?_
We have the highest number of uninsured people in the country, including children. Families are struggling to pay bills and put food on the table. We rank too low on education for a state that should be leading the nation. But Abbott’s donors and the insiders who stay close to power are doing just fine.
**We can’t afford another four years of that. And Abbott knows it.**
He will do everything in his power to protect his grip on Texas — and he has the money and the influence to help him.
So this is our chance to meet the moment and do everything we can to help Gina win.
[**If you are ready to build on this momentum and help Gina defeat Greg Abbott in November, will you split $5 or any amount between Small Town PAC and Gina to power her campaign for governor?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20260529-707&t=3&akid=707%2E34582%2EYYJ1ia)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=20260529-707&t=22&akid=707%2E34582%2EYYJ1ia)**
Let’s make this happen, Peter.
Thank you,
Beto

Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to build a Democratic Party that invests in small towns and delivers a message that resonates with rural America.
Together, we're finding and recruiting thoughtful, hardworking people to run for office, and supporting a new generation of leaders who truly reflect and understand their communities.
**[It’s time for Democrats to expand the map and put small towns back at the forefront: pitch in now to help build our movement from the ground up.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/stp-ms-em-footer?refcode=em20260529-707&t=23&refcode2=707_34582_YYJ1ia&akid=707%2E34582%2EYYJ1ia)**

Republican Task Force Issue: 5/29/2026
Iran Deal on Trump's Desk

US and Iranian negotiators [reached an agreement](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0D-vpSAQBfBPgx0Gx78UFNvY3W23NCMzKFlEgtzrfvyNr3n966aYnJzf-fNaXuiDj9tvPNjk4hY6afEZIzEGLDtGAgUTMdLOuICCQapegl5iWJqKDFnCxlZsmnFSSutGN9VugMe-sxqHdZhgol47btkNDkZe7ei6ypsnSvWgoe11N9XQduic7oeh72DVregUBs6lzpzea_AWY8Hrrzuz5dqeRxXMXkq6RPtLwCxgvu-7XsN5Hivn7fkQMEe-LwEz5uJt4Of8BgiY35d8qDIz2l0-YnlGyf8KR2KSlvFi5zPLxJF83GTJ7yNJTCmfHwxVNpRuH4K_hlF0ajvQh69u5QdTfgz8DwAA__-QDYIf) Thursday to extend the ceasefire 60 days and begin formal nuclear talks. Trump entered the Situation Room Friday morning to make a final determination on the deal. VP Vance [told reporters](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O5CAQhJ_GzhhBGzAEBJdMNpdeaLXpZowO_wgzO9q3X3keYcNSSVX6vn-P6YG55O35F1cOtaWJdppyxY0YC7YFNwIJjhhpYZxAghXSCPDTVibVU6BIqGLPQY1OSu-VV_0SpEnkR0bW2tFsAdA6JV2avTJek-lzuKakAQ-D8drdYNCYkjfWGg2zHzotsXBtt8rHay454tbw_J_2GvkW97UvYWntOLvhTwf3Du54bPw-r-oKteVYuIP7xSJep3hjFXsuYsVvAU58QFwyTODUMKMdKI3IPsaZvVfWOQLf10DHO5eSTzt2Wj5XzOVz3n7h6ivATwAAAP__rUNzXQ) both sides are "very close" but the outcome remains "still TBD." Iran has declared its right to enrich uranium a non-negotiable red line — a sticking point unresolved as of this writing. A deal would ease oil market pressure and avert wider regional conflict. A breakdown risks renewed hostilities along the Strait of Hormuz, and [ABC News reports](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGO8yAQhJ8Gd0SwYGMKil_6ZemKXHultcA6RiHYwiR5_ZOvuvraGWlmvvm6zldMOZXbJz7I1bbMcYtzqlgiYca2YokgYIyEcSWcQcDARc_BziXPsosuhogydOSkGYWwVlrZrc4MGtQgRNBeKRmCtMYr4wepaBE-6i65M0r0YEH1Vo8XUBqXxfbD0GvwVjEtMFNtl0r70-cUsDQ87stWA13C9uiyW1vbD6b-MZgYTOhDofdxegymj9KoFmxpK5gZTDm9iD_3iI0OBtNJyH9rfCcMxE9q_t7qne91u1U6Dl6fPm1nhZpSZOq_VArMKIzpqov7O-WcjsEwLW4PTPlnWvvDky8H3wEAAP__VPeAKA) negotiations remain fluid heading into the weekend. ★★★
'Weaponization' Fund Frozen

A federal judge in Virginia [temporarily blocked](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJycULuOpDAQ_BrIjExjMzhwcAnZXHohauhm8I2xkW0O3X79ik0237AeKlXVn-f0ROddeP3GnW0q60SRJpcwEKPHsmEgkDAQI22ME0johdQCzBT81NZkaSFsl5pt-xikNKY1bb1ZpbuHNqgkI8y8kNJoZrUS0dwyrX3t7B0lNRjotFFDA53CdTW677WC2XSVkug5lSbxcc7eLRgK5vca08LNEvfa262UI1fdrwrGCsbruprEZ-GUb_1mYvJUwXhm8fekF4vC-xETJuf_i9nH5Z1FSed-ZNEOYnbeuxjExXjE4D6w3Gg9A4nv1RWMdbJ0XLc5949KydeOzn81Kj848J-FzwAAAP__s0d_NA) the Trump DOJ's $1.8 billion "Anti-Weaponization Fund" Friday — created to compensate alleged victims of government overreach as part of a settlement of Trump's own IRS lawsuit. The freeze halts disbursements while the court weighs legal challenges. [Critics have called](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFuxCAQheHT4I4VjG3WFBRp3G3alNbADDYJiy2Mk-tHmyOkftKnp__jsTww5VTWd3yyqy0utNOSKhZizNg2LAQKJmKkjXEBBUaqUYJdSl50R44CoQ4dO32flLJWW91tzseegp9s8GYy4NWg2VpPd9MrzWS5S-5FqREs9KMdphv0A8ZoR2PGAbztxaAwc223ysflcwpYGp5fca-Bb2F_dtltrR2n6N8EzALmtvGWcn5tAubK65Wxpb0ImMN-1SY9tpb5FDCP9vXUyMjEFbP8vGhleeB18injVUjA3FVHx0_KOZ3mLga1PjH94V37R6dvB78BAAD__4rVdVg) the fund a slush fund for Trump allies rather than a legitimate compensation mechanism for government overreach victims. The administration has defended the fund as a tool for Americans wrongly targeted by federal agencies. The ruling adds another [judicial obstacle](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGunTAQBNCvMZ2RWWzAhYs0dDdtSrSwy8W5xkbGBClf_8T7hNeNNNLRaP68phf64OP7N-7sclknSjT5jJEYA5YNI4GCgRhpY5xAQSeVkWCnGKamIkcLYbNU7Jp-UMraxjbV5pRhi6zWthn0rJthJkJUrRr61mia-8q7h1IGLLTG6qGGVuO6WtN1RsNsW6EVBs6lznxcc_ALxoLnZ0154XpJexXcVspxivaXgFHAeN93vcT4dALGRxcwKvNkK2A8UvDFL6eAcWXijEH-vejNcsNQTnmn_JEpypKv_TglxuLlzXik6P9j8SnK9YpUZUfH7UPwZ9cLrd47-vC9pvzgvH8OvgIAAP__fVt8LA) for a White House that has faced scores of court challenges since January. ★★★
Mail Voting Order Stands

A federal judge [declined Thursday](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O5CAQhJ8GZ4xw-2cgILjE2Vx6odWmmwEdBgvjnddfeR9h4yqV6vv-vdYXxhTz-y_ubGvzKxVaY8VMjAlbwEygQBMjBcYVFMxSTRLMmtPad2TJEfauY9s_tVLG9KbvgmWtcHbeee5p2ny_6Xn0z8HQplE7P3TR3lNqAgPDZEb9gGFE7800z9MImxnEqDBxbY_Kx7Wl6DA3PP_7Uh0_XNm7ZENrxymGPwIWAUsLHGJKdyZgCWXnzJ9TwIK0xxzPVrHFkgUskzbaGC1duWqT9br5ZavXfsgdY5Ixyw1TKk2WSlwFLF21dHxiSvGcn2JU77v386L9QtqXhe8AAAD__59gezY) to block Trump's executive order tightening mail-in voting rules — handing the administration a legal win on election integrity as implementation moves forward. The order enlists the Postal Service in a national voter eligibility check. Judge Carl Nichols ruled that [Democrats' challenge](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDFyhiAUhE-DHQ4-RaWgSGP3p03pPOGpJAgOoub4GVPkAKm_2Z3d7-M1vtB5F5Z33EinPI822tElDJbQY14xWBDQW0K7Eo4goOVCclBj8GNVWG2NxcoUpKuuF0KpSlXFqmlqewFS9hMQdWIWqjPYtTP1cqong4XTT5WQoKCWqulLqBucZyXbVjYwqZo1Aj2lXCbaz8k7gyHj8TXHZKg0cSu8XnPeD1a_MRgYDPd9l4nOTOl4OIPB04KewbDEi1LYKGQGw-dpF-LofbwPntO57dxtu6cH8w2d5y7wK2YXFk7fZM7sLuIxWUr8733PYCiStvvtvHdH27FGLE_4d1n-h8hLw08AAAD__0o2ga8) was premature, leaving the order fully in effect. The decision is a notable legal victory for the administration's election integrity agenda. [AP News reports](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LGO5CAQBNCvsTNG0AYbAoJLJptLL7TaTTNGh7GFmZn9_JX3EzYslfRUqn-P-YEpp_L8ixv72uIc9jCniiUwZmwrlgASbGAMK-MMEkYhjQA3lzyrPvhAARX17NVkpXROOdWvnqQ0egLUcUBCpdHYSMEoMmwH66Y--YuSBhwMxml7g0FjjM6Mo9GwuKHTEjPXdqt8vJacCEvD83_cK_GN9q3Pfm3tOLvhTwf3Du54FP6cV3WF2hJl7uDe6ms7BGemlvZyig1TFu-9pfIU_MX0aunNYq-Bq3B60hFZKzWqQMYZDc4gq2GSCy3W9tWH45NyTuc4dVo-L-xnTPvFd28P3wEAAP__gjh7Bg) the ruling could reshape mail-in voting procedures ahead of the 2026 midterms.
* * *
GOP Rallies Behind Paxton

Senate Republicans are closing ranks behind Ken Paxton in Texas, following his victory over John Cornyn. Talarico has outraised him and opened a Houston general-election launch [targeting Paxton's past](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFytSAUhJ8GOx08gkhB8Td2929TOkc4XpkgOMCNydtnTJM-3RY73-58b4_lgT74-PyPB5lct8Ult_iM0REGrDtGBxwmR-h2wgU4jC2XLeglhqVvnHHWYW8bMr2aONe6132zm1FvcpSOxKiGlSSCclz0QqpVkeCwNd7cKC5BwyC1mDoYBG6bluMoBax6YIJjoFy7TOdrDd5irFjet5QtdTYdTTB7rWdhwz8GM4P5uq7uTMFXb9NdYDBHugqD-V5iMHN554nB_IssbaVPLO2RIn21NkVLOZZ2xVoDPXN6RVdazvWggasmG3dePgRfRsUEfx7ow8-X-gd1Hwa-AwAA__8PRnoG) -- leaving the GOP to hope unity compensates for cash.

★★★
Rubio Closes Gap on Vance

The latest Emerson poll puts Vance and Rubio at 28% and 27% respectively in a hypothetical 2028 primary -- statistically tied. Rubio's Iran diplomacy has boosted his standing, while [Pete Buttigieg leads](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFuhDAQheHTmM4rM2BgChdp6DZtSjTYA1gxtmW8u8rto80RUj_pk97_dV_u5IOP-yedbErdFpfc4gtFxxSoHhQdKJgckzuYFlAwSKUl4BLD0jbOOOuotQ2bdpyUQmyxbQ6D06CHrbe4cW9HACI74sqdBQStBmy8eVNKA0KnsZ9u0PW0baiHQfewYid6RYFLvRXOjzV4S7HS9b2lYvlm09kEc9SaL9F9CJgFzPXgw4fw3gTMRzo58usSMFs6M_k9Cpj1hJNSk3xfknvKMhd_UvmRT4qWZXmsPsmcQhAwN8W4_PIh-GsYRa_2k_yf3tR_hHoa-A0AAP__85x0LA) the Democratic field at 18%.

★★★
GOP Hunts for a Midterm Message

House Republicans are heading into the midterms without a coherent message, torn between defending Trump's agenda and pivoting to fiscal themes. With Democrats [up nine points](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2SpSAUhJ8GMy08IFcCgk3M7qYbWocf9dQiWMCMrz_lJJNP1kF3f139772-kSKl_S-ewZS2rT77lQomHzBiOzB54DD7gP4IuAIH1fOpB72muI6dN955HF0XzPiaOdd61GN3GGvnIDRKKxSiBRSz4MEit8oGJ4XqyDxVfAINYtJyHkBI3DY9KTVJsFowyTGG0oYSrg8byWFqWP9vubgwuHx20RytXZWJPwwWBst938ON9aC0t5yuXNtjY7BcOVIjVxksD5PBwqdHz0_owNZjCf0PpfZ7prT3Ds8LaU8Mlq4Yf90UI1X1YpLvJ1L8HtF-8dmnga8AAAD__zLdeT8) on the generic ballot and approval at record lows, the identity crisis runs deep.

* * *
Iran War Powers Vote Pulled

House GOP leaders yanked a scheduled vote on an [Iran war powers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O4yAUhZ_G7ojgGv9QUGyTLttuaV3DJUbBgADH2rcfZZrppz7SOef7_j3WB_rg4_MvHqRLc6tNdvUFoyUM2HaMFjgsltDuhCtwmBgfGag1hlX0VltjUZietJgXzpUSSvS75jCjkWIglE6hXKxzYjbjNqt5E9ap3utPFR9BwTAqudxgkOicGqdplLCpoZMcA5V2K5TPLXiDsWF9uVQM3Uw6-qD31nLthj8d3Du4R7rqRfT6hB3c65kLHcRMOktjB_5nZ6ZomUnxWahWltNFhaU3FdbKeeTKPtjswsJ-JisTwLkcFPRF23z5EHyd5k7y54E-fB9pv_D21vAVAAD__zLSfMo) resolution Friday -- short on votes to defeat it. The bipartisan measure would have reasserted congressional war authority. Some members want SCOTUS to rule on the statute's constitutionality.

★★★
GOP Redraws the Map

Republicans are pursuing aggressive redistricting in southern states after court rulings weakened the Voting Rights Act. Democrats, expecting to lose House seats, are [reportedly weighing](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFyhCAYhJ8GOxz8FYSCIo3dpU3p_MLPyQTRQe6cvH3GPEK6LXZ299uvx_zAmGJ-fuJGttQw-93PsWD2hAnritmDAO0J_Uo4gwDFheRg5pzmrvHWO4-da8h2oxbCmM50zWqDGDuQY-ecozF4ckHggsH0o1y01qqJ9o4SEgz00gy6hX7AEIxUSg6wmJ4NAhOV2hY6XkuKDnPF8zvsxVHr9q1Jdq31OFn_wWBiMF3X1R57ijW6_TYwmDJdJ4PpbmIwCXlrzWB6F-TldWPzi-JzPfmeuaft5DcrP0rcsPxwh4myx8KFML1RSjbF-uOKKcVTjWwQzw1j-htT__Hd28JvAAAA___hgHm5) front-loading two southern states in the 2028 primary calendar to preserve regional leverage.

★★★
Anti-Weaponization Fund Divides GOP

Trump's DOJ stood up a $1.8 billion [anti-weaponization fund](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGu3CAQRb8Gd1h4bLymoEjjbtOmtMYwrEkwIGDXUr4-cqT3A6-aIx1pZu799dye6IOPr594ki7NbTbZzReMljBgOzBaELBYQnsQbiBg5kJyUFsM29BZbY3FwXSkh8cihFKDGrpD4wSKrJyNtA4JhBPOmN0JpHkhuYvO63uVkKBglGpaehgndE7JeZYT7Gpkk8BApfWF8nsP3mBsWP-4VAz1Jp1d0EdrubLxB4OVwXpdV-9S2anemsFafaN6TyxoU4kM1vsmg1XImxcGayvvM1eOOZf0wcALNh9f_PCt8kImFctDuriPHGNqBxWeUwgcb_v11s2_yTSOsXl-EeYU_V9sPkXu3tEyWLuibb58CL7ODzaJ14k-_E_RvlH6R8O_AAAA__9ifJIw) from his IRS settlement -- but some congressional Republicans are pushing back. Converting a personal presidential lawsuit into a government compensation fund strikes even allies as constitutionally fraught.
